customer_reviews.title: Great jeans if you want a slimmer, tighter fit than the normal version
customer_reviews.text: I've become a big fan of these jeans. I've always had Levis, but decided to try these 18 months ago to see how the classic Wrangler jeans looked with my cowboy boots. At that point I had about a dozen pairs of Levis - now, I'm down to two pairs of Levis and eleven pairs of these Wrangler 936 slim fit jeans. That's how much I like them!There's a lot of reviews here saying these jeans are tight, and they are (they're meant to be), but I think some reviewers are perhaps being a little optimistic with their sizing. I wear a 30" waist in Levis and have found that these Wranglers fit me snugly in a 31" waist size, and very snugly with a 30" waist size, but are still not at all uncomfortable. In fact I have both sizes, depending on the look I'm going for - the 31s fit perfectly through the hips and seat, snug but not tight. The 30s however fit me nice and tight in the same areas, as well as being much tighter through the thighs. Both are comfortable but I can feel the 30s pulling everything in as I zip them up, which should give an idea of how they fit. There is certainly no room for bulky underwear and perhaps that's the mistake some people are making with their designer boxers - I'm not an underwear fashion victim however and my "tighty whitey" briefs work absolutely fine with these jeans. The legs are quite trim but go perfectly over the tops of my cowboy boots, I never tuck them into my boots but they are skinny enough to do so if that's your look. The waist is fairly high and looks good with a tucked-in T-shirt and nice belt - I do think those who have a bit of a belly might feel this makes them feel too tight also, but being in my twenties and still managing to hold onto my flat stomach I can't really comment. I may change my mind in a couple of decades, but as it stands, I would agree with a previous reviewer's slightly blunt suggestion that these are really cut to provide a tight fit for boys rather than larger men - so whilst they fit my small frame very nicely, bigger guys looking for a comfier fit would be better off with the 13MWZ version.Quality and detail is nice, perhaps some of the stitching doesn't appear to be on a par with Levis (especially round the crotch) but I've yet to have a pair show any signs of failure. The various colours are nicely finished and (again, unlike some reviewers) I actually quite like the Wrangler patch on the back. Yes, it's plastic and not leather, but that kind-of goes with the simple and basic nature of these jeans. The seven belt loops even on the 30" size is a plus, although not strictly necessary on my small waist I'm sure it helps on the larger sizes. The two front belt loops are a little closer together than I'd like with some of my chunkier belts but it doesn't look out of place and, again, a larger waist will probably not suffer this issue. Other details like the extra rivets and bold "W"s on the pockets are distinctive. The material has a soft and tactile feel entirely missing from my recent Levis, although I should point out that the "rigid" indigo versions of these are made of a much stiffer material. Not unpleasant, just different. With eleven pairs, I have these in most of the available colours and my favourites are the Rough Stone and Charcoal Grey ones, although the bleach ones are a particularly cool colour too.In summary then, great jeans. I always used to find Wranglers a bit "cheesy" as a Levis-wearing kid, but now I wish I'd discovered these years ago. Far better for less money, what more could you want!

customer_reviews.title: For the 936PWD Style!
customer_reviews.text: My husband has been a Wrangler man for probably the last 10 years. He used to be a hardcore Levi's guy, until their prices became ridiculous and the denim started completely wearing out after just a couple months of use.We used to go with the unwashed denim, for longer wear, but honestly, they were such a hassle and always got odd creases in them even with the most strict following of the instructions that we just decided to go with the PWD, which stands for Pre-Washed Denim.Things to note about the Cowboy Cut 936pwd style:1) These pants are supposed to fit at your natural waist, not your hips! Your natural waist is above your hip bones, and USUALLY can be found in line with the middle of your belly button. If you don't know how to find your natural waist, look it up- lots of helpful pics and articles.2) These pants are supposed to fit snugly! They are not supposed to be baggy at all.3) These pants may shrink a bit, so if you are on the edge of sizing up because these are already a bit uncomfortable, size up!4.) These pants fit best on people/men who are long and lean. I say this because they are so snug, and sit at your natural waist. Some may find this too constricting.My husband does manual labor for a living as a glazier. Wranglers have been awesome at protecting his legs from some crazy scary glass shards that have ripped other people's sissy brand pants to shreds. They have always been well worth the cost. A pair of Wranglers typically will last my husband about a year and a half to two years depending on how many he has on rotation. During lean times, if he only has, say 3 pair on rotation, they may last about a year due to the increased wash and wear. I recently splurged when I saw that Amazon had an amazing price on these babies, putting them at less than half of retail. So I bought 6 for less than I would have in store for 3. Sweet!!If you are a lean person like my husband, who looks like they are wearing their older and bigger sibling's pants when you try on Original fit or Relaxed fit and you DON'T want to look disheveled/unprofessional, these pants are for you.  They look tailor-made to fit your body, and they are classy and professional looking.No butt bling, or saggy britches showing off your boxers here! These here are real man's pants.I have pictures of a pair that he has been wearing for about 6 months, that we purchased in store, compared to a pair I bought from Amazon, brand new out of the box.Note that the older pair have shrunk by about 2 inches. Now, I didn't measure the store bought ones when we brought them home, but they always fit him a little long and then after a few weeks of wash, they fit just right in the length.The only difference in the two pair is that the store bought ones were made in Mexico of U.S denim, and the ones I purchased from Amazon are made in Nicaragua from U.S. denim. Not sure if Wrangler switched their manufacturer (again) or if they have different manufacturing places for different sellers.I have already washed these several times and they have been in his rotation for about a month. They have conformed nicely as expected to his frame, and he has expressed no complaints.All in all, if you want some nice, presentable pants that are professional looking, durable as all get out, or maybe some nice jeans for Sunday dinners, church, or a night out, look no further!

customer_reviews.title: These Might Be The PERFECT Jeans For Guys Like Me!
customer_reviews.text: UPDATE 9/2023: I finally had to wash these, and was sad to find that they do shrink in the wash. So the 30 inch length that was perfect for me before washing is now too short. They're also less soft now that I've washed them. I will order a new pair in the 32 length and try to get the length tailored since they aren't offered in a 31 inch length.Seriously, finding jeans like these is like finding the pot of gold at the end of the rainbow. It's virtually impossible, so it feels almost miraculous when it does happen.I have decently large thighs (from cycling and other things), and calves, and a decent size rear. Most men's jeans are too straight, so they're too tight across the thighs (showing pocket lines and underwear lines), or too saggy in the butt, or the legs are just plain too tight, or they're too baggy and look messy.I'm a tall, muscular guy with a decently athletic build. I don't claim to be a model or anything, but pants shouldn't look as sloppy on me as they tend to. I shouldn't have to pick between pants that fit like skinny jeans and pants that make me look like I have absolutely no sense of fashion (i.e. the infamous baggy, shapeless, dad jean fit). I see tall, muscular guys in movies and tv shows that have great fitting jeans that complement their muscular builds without looking like skinny jeans, and I think to myself people love this look, so why can't I find that pants that fit like that?It turns out, pants like that do exist. These Levi's 541 Athletic Fit pants in the Native Cali color fit, feel, and look amazing. They're beautifully manly pants, without being too cowboy or too hip. They're very neutral, allow you to wear them with leather dress shoes, boots, or sneakers, without looking too weird.The fit around the hips/but is great, with enough room for them to sit where you want them to (not low-cut skinny jeans or saggy hipster jeans), so you shouldn't have issues with plumber's crack, as long as you get the right fit and wear a belt.The fit around the thighs is also great. Depending on what size you order, they have enough room that they don't show pocket lines or underwear lines, and unlike many pants, they're actually cut in such a way that if the pants fit well at the waist, the thighs aren't too tight. These come in 1 inch sizes, you can experiment to find the right fit for you. I find that both the 36 and the 35 waist fit me well. The 35 I do fold up the pockets to avoid pocket lines, and that size gives me more of a custom-made for me look. The 36 has a little more room, so the lines aren't an issue so far, but they aren't quite so fitted, but they also aren't straying into dad-jean territory.I also love that even though they have extra room in the seat and thighs, they aren't too tight in the calves, OR too wide and shapeless at the ankle. As I mentioned, my legs are different widths at the thigh, knees, calves, AND ankles, so finding jeans that fit ok in all places is incredible. The fit being right at the ankles makes for a nice modern look that can work with a variety of footwear. If the ankles were wider, they would splay out at the show and give more a bootcut or dad-jean look that doesn't look good with sneakers or other snappy fits.The one downside is that the length varies. I had to buy two pairs of the same length to find one that fit right. The other pair was slightly too short.I haven't washed these yet, and I'm reluctant to do so until I really have to. It's possible that doing so will change my rating. But right now, they fit perfectly, and the color is so black that I can wear these with a formal black vest and a button down and it looks great. I'm sure the dye will fade over time the more I wear these, and then they'll become more casual-wear jeans. But for now I love these just the way they are.

customer_reviews.title: Great pants, but more variety in fit from wash to wash than I'd expect
customer_reviews.text: Ordered these because, like many others here, I've got bigger thighs and a butt that are the limiting factor on the cuts of jeans I can wear.  I was specifically looking for jeans that can be appropriate for work and evenings.  I was a little hesitant after seeing some reviews here talking about the different material ratios and fits of the different colors.  I can confirm that this is accurate, but that's something that's pretty common when you're talking about jeans.  I did, however, expect that after looking at the Levi's website, seeing which washes had the 98/2 cotton/elastane ratio that those washes would fit the same.  That wasn't the case either though, and that's why I'm giving them 4 instead of 5 stars.The two colors I went with at first were the Midnight and the Timberwolf.  Both arrived with tags that marked them as "stretch," which made me feel kind of weird.  They both do, in fact, have a bit of give to them, but you don't have to worry about them looking or feeling like you're putting on yoga pants.  They are roomy where they need to be while looking neat and thus can be used for work like I wanted.  However, I'd say that the Midnight wash was slightly larger than I was expecting while the Timberwolf were somewhat smaller, or rather, they just fit more snugly than the Midnight ones.  They're probably closer to what I expected the size to be, but it was odd that there was any difference for two pairs of pants supposedly in the same line (541) and made from the same material "98% Cotton, 2% Elastane."Regardless, they still both were cut the way I was looking for in terms of their general shape if not necessarily the specific fit on the waist.  Color-wise, the Midnight pair look exactly as pictured, while the Timberwolf are darker than what's pictured above.  The Levi's site has a more accurate color for them if you take a look there.  I prefer the color I received to what I saw above, but just know they will be darker.I also wanted a darker blue pair, but did not read good things about The Rich or Rigid Dragon here.  I was apprehensive, but decided to try The Rich to see for myself.  I was pleasantly surprised.  They're definitely a fit closer to the Timberwolf than the Midnight, which I guess is why some people said they're a bit more "rigid" but I've had those rough old Levi's in the past and these are certainly not anything close to that.  They also look like they're going to bleed, so I'm going to need to do the whole cold water + vinegar wash on them before I wear them.Overall these are good pants for anyone with a build that's got more meat in the butt/thigh region and struggling to find comfortable and stylish jeans in the straight or slim(mer) style.  Just be mindful that not all the washes are created equal in terms of the fit or feel and that there may be some color deviations from what you see above.

Based on another review, I took a chance on these XXL and they're perfect.  The color - khaki - is just what I wanted, and the material seems like good quality.  The elastic waistband fits comfortably snug on my 34/35-inch waist, but the drawstring helps if you want a tighter fit.  And it even has belt loops if you want a belted look.  I also like that they have back pockets that button if I'm carrying a wallet.  They're obviously quite a bit baggier than I would normally wear, but that's what I was going for with these: casual, lightweight, comfy for a beach wedding vow renewal. Here's where I ran into some problems. The pants I received fit perfectly in the waist. The length, although wearable, is a little shorter than I like. I didn't wash the pants, but if they ever shrink, then I really won't be able to comfortably wear them at a shorter length. I think the waist would probably be ok. Narrowing the leg of the pant would probably help give a different look to the pants. When I compared the length of these pants to the other brand I bought, there was only about a 1/2 inch difference in length. However, the other brand is more of a tapered leg and looks way longer to the eye despite the very minor difference in length. I'm not sure if the short pant length is relegated to this particular pair, since other reviewers said the pants they received were long? I may try another pair to see if they come longer next time? The overall cut is fuller, so it looks weird to have a short pant leg. Overall, I like the quality of the pants and would recommend them provided you receive a size that fits properly. I was disappointed because I like the large color selection and the quality of these. Hopefully, my next pair will come a little longer?

Like a lot of people seem to thing, but have the look and feel of quality linen, but without the shrinkage. Cons...meah, slightly more tapered at the leg, but then its resort wear so casual is what's the haps. I might argue for one more inch at the hem, but it still clear the ankle. Pros...Fit/Size perfect. I am a 36w X 32L and that's exactly what I got with room to spare or shrink, preferably shrink a bit. Multiple colors, not just tan, white, blue. Looks great rolled up or with deck shoes. To conclude, this is a good solid buy. And much more economical that other linen brands. Looking forwards to seeing how well they wear and last. I'm kind of a clothes snob, but like putting together outfits that are cheap but look amazing. So giving this a 5 star rating for looks, fitting, versatility, and most defiantly cost.

customer_reviews.title: Fit + construction + price = perfection
customer_reviews.text: Ok, I’m not sure why anyone would leave a negative review or why these are high return items, but my experience has been exceptional. My son had been wearing his regular jeans to work (landscaping) and was absolutely destroying them. He needed work pants and he’s hard to fit (29x34) because he’s tall and lanky. I didn’t have a lot of money to spend and because of his odd size, I came straight to Amazon. These pants appeared on my second swipe up and I saw that one color was on sale for $9.99. I originally ordered him 3 pairs of the sale pants, but ordered him 30x34’s because that’s what he wanted. Got them in 2 days with my Prime and they were perfect for his needs, though he needed a 29” waist.  My son loves how comfortable they are and he says they’re much cooler than jeans. He can wear the 30’s, but I decided to order him some in his regular size of 29x34. I will say that he probably could have gone down to 33” length, possibly 32”, but with his cowboy boots, the 34” are fine. I’m thinking the pants might be slightly big in the waist and length measurements, so you might want to order one size smaller in both dimensions. They aren’t huge, just maybe an inch bigger. So here I go to order more pants and I saw there were 2 additional colors on sale except these were $6.62. What?!?! I couldn’t believe it! I immediately ordered him 6 additional pairs, 4 of one color and 2 of the other. Those 6 pairs were less than $10 more in total than my first order. I couldn’t believe it because I already knew the pants were well made. They hold up very well during washing and they don’t wrinkle. (Hallelujah!)  I mean can you imagine a better deal? The pants are appropriate for dinner, church, work (any kind), really anywhere you’d wear a pair of khakis. I could not be happier with this purchase and urge you to buy them if you’re on the fence. They are totally worth the price, especially if you catch an amazing sale like I did. You’ll be amazed at the quality versus price point and if you manage to get them for $6.62 it’ll make your day! Make sure you check all the colors because they don’t all cost the same. You don’t want to miss an opportunity to get them at rock bottom prices. Trust me, buy them! You won’t regret it.

customer_reviews.title: A Mediocre Choice
customer_reviews.text: I recently purchased the Dockers Men's Straight Fit Signature Lux Cotton Stretch Khaki Pant and have mixed feelings about its overall performance. While it does have a few positive aspects, there are several areas where it falls short. In this thorough and detailed review, I will provide honest and unbiased feedback based on my personal experience, covering all key points that potential buyers should consider.Fit and Comfort: ⭐⭐⭐When it comes to fit, the Dockers Men's Straight Fit Khaki Pant delivers decently. The waist and inseam measurements were accurate, and the straight fit style provided a comfortable amount of room without being too baggy. However, the cotton stretch material, touted as a luxurious feature, did not live up to its claims. It felt rather stiff and lacked the desired flexibility, making movements restrictive at times. Although the pant loosened up slightly after a few washes, it still didn't match the level of comfort I had expected.Quality and Durability: ⭐⭐⭐The overall quality of the Dockers Khaki Pant is satisfactory, but it doesn't quite meet the standards I would expect from a reputable brand like Dockers. The stitching is neat and secure, but the fabric itself is prone to wrinkling and loses its shape easily, requiring frequent ironing to maintain a presentable appearance. The durability is average, as I noticed some signs of wear after just a few months of regular use. It is not a pant that would withstand heavy-duty activities, but for casual wear, it should hold up reasonably well.Style and Versatility: ⭐⭐⭐⭐One area where the Dockers Khaki Pant shines is its style and versatility. It features a classic design that can be dressed up or down for various occasions. The straight fit gives a polished look, making it suitable for both formal and casual settings. The range of available colors is impressive, allowing you to find a shade that matches your personal style. Whether you pair it with a dress shirt or a simple t-shirt, this pant can adapt to different outfits, making it a versatile addition to any wardrobe.Maintenance and Care: ⭐⭐Taking care of the Dockers Khaki Pant requires some extra effort. The fabric is not as low-maintenance as I had hoped. It tends to attract lint and pet hair easily, making it necessary to use a lint roller before wearing it. Additionally, the recommended washing instructions suggest machine washing on a delicate cycle, which can be inconvenient for individuals who prefer a more straightforward laundry routine. Moreover, the fabric's tendency to wrinkle means you'll have to invest time in ironing if you want a crisp appearance. Overall, the maintenance and care required for these pants can be a hassle.Value for Money: ⭐⭐⭐In terms of value for money, the Dockers Khaki Pant falls into the average category. While it offers some style and versatility, the overall quality and comfort leave room for improvement. Considering the price point, I expected a higher level of durability and better fabric performance. There are other brands on the market that offer similar or even better quality at a lower price. If you're solely looking for a basic pair of khaki pants, it may be worth exploring more affordable alternatives before committing to the Dockers Men's Straight Fit Signature Lux Cotton Stretch Khaki Pant.Conclusion:In conclusion, the Dockers Men's Straight Fit Signature Lux Cotton Stretch Khaki Pant is a somewhat disappointing choice. It has its positive aspects, such as its versatile style and decent fit, but it falls short in terms of comfort, fabric quality, and durability. The maintenance and care required for these pants can be a hassle for those seeking a low-maintenance option. Considering the price, there are better alternatives available in the market. If you prioritize comfort and long-lasting quality, I would recommend exploring other options before settling on this particular pant.

customer_reviews.title: Tapered leg beach pant
customer_reviews.text: I purchased three pairs of these for a cruise to the Bahamas. The fit is the best thing about these linen blend pants. In comparison to other brands I have purchased, these have a tapered leg and less voluminous overall fit. Are these skinny fit? No...so don't misunderstand. I never understand why people expect a beach pant to be skinny, when the point is to wear a loose, cool pant for the hot weather? I bought white, navy and beige and all have a nice weight to the fabric. They're not flimsy feeling or see-thru like some others I tried. As other reviewers have stated, the beige is slightly yellowish and the navy is slightly lighter than navy. The color difference isn't a deal breaker for me, so I kept all three. The pockets are patch pockets, which give them a casual vibe. I like the dressier look of non-patch pockets on another brand I bought at the same time, but this is the only brand I've found that's more fitted. After washing the pants in gentle, cool water and line drying, I didn't notice any shrinkage. For reference, I wear a 32x32 jean and size 32 fit perfectly in length and waist. The only negative about these pants involves the beige color pant. I experienced the same problem as another reviewer. When the beige pant was washed, it looked like the color was bleached out of the fabric over a large area. I thought I overused the oxyclean when I tried to remove some stains from the trip. However, after drying, the color was perfectly normal over the entire pant with no problems. I definitely recommend these pants.

customer_reviews.title: Good look and fit!
customer_reviews.text: I was looking for something very inexpensive to get for my teenager's job interview endeavors. This was a great purchase. I bought two, one in large and one in medium because its so hard to know with buying clothes online if it will truly fit well. The medium fit him perfectly (with a tad bit of room to spare) so I bought a second pair in medium and returned the large. I love that if he were to gain ten pounds in the next two months (hopefully not but just saying) that these will still fit comfortably. Return process was easy. So far I recommend this seller and these pants, and I'll update later if we discover the quality wasn't as great our initial impression. The only downside to them was the material is the kind that dog and cat hair will stick to like a magnet but we use lint rollers so non issue. If you don't have pets no worries. If you do, don't let them get on ya before heading out. Put them on right before you leave and then you'll avoid hairy pants, lol. These are priced really well for the good features and fit. I did get them on sale and paid about $21 for them. If he really likes the comfortability of these and wants more, Id even pay the regular $29 price as long as they're durable for the job (indoor jobs only – they're not a thick material) But Im always looking for a deal so Im super happy getting these on sale.

The length is long but cuffing them doesn’t look bad. I had to cuff them twice.I saw people complaining about how long the crotch is but that’s because these are not low rise pants. customer_reviews.title: A Note on Sizing
customer_reviews.text: First off, these pants are exactly what I'd envisioned.  Very light but seem to be well built. What I'm going to do is buy a pair of 3X, wash and dry them, and see what the end result is and I'll post those results. customer_reviews.title: I Bought Three Pair of These Great Pants- They Say I’ve Given Up... in Style
customer_reviews.text: Hanes ComfortSoft EcoSmart Men's Fleece Sweatpants are basically the official uniform for anyone who’s decided that regular pants are just an unnecessary societal construct. These sweatpants aren’t just clothing—they’re a lifestyle choice, one that says, “I could do real pants, but why?”First Impressions:The moment you slip into these bad boys, it’s like your legs have been given their own personal cloud to lounge on. Seriously, I’m pretty sure these sweatpants are softer than my hopes and dreams. And the fleece? Oh man, it’s like a hug from a really cozy bear who’s also really into saving the environment, because these pants are EcoSmart, after all. That’s right, you’re saving the planet—in sweatpants. Take that, jeans!The Fit:Let’s talk fit. These pants are roomy. Like, “I could fit an extra sandwich in my pocket and you wouldn’t even know” roomy. They’ve got that classic “I’ve completely abandoned all attempts at impressing anyone” vibe, but in a way that’s kind of charming. The waistband is adjustable, so whether you’ve just finished a workout or just finished a pizza (no judgment), these pants will expand or contract to match your life choices. Elastic cuffs? Oh yeah, you bet. They’re keeping things in place, but not too tight—just tight enough to remind you that you’re still a functioning human.Fashion Forward?Fashionable? Well, let’s just say no one’s going to mistake these for runway couture, but who cares? Sweatpants don’t need to be fashionable. They’re timeless. Whether you’re working from home, binge-watching a show, or just staring out the window wondering when it’s acceptable to take a nap, these pants are the perfect companion. Plus, they come in multiple colors, so you can technically have one for each day of the week. That’s basically the same as putting effort into your wardrobe, right?Durability:These things are built to last. I’m pretty sure they’d survive an apocalypse. You could probably wear them every day for a month straight (no judgment if you do), and they’d still hold up. Plus, they’re EcoSmart, which means they’re made with recycled materials. So not only are you avoiding real pants, but you’re also helping save the planet. Talk about multitasking!The Comfy Test:I did a “Comfy Test,” which involves lying on the couch in various positions for hours and seeing if the pants pass. Spoiler: they absolutely do. Sitting, slouching, sprawling—these pants support it all. I’m pretty sure they could double as pajamas if I weren’t already living in them during the day.

customer_reviews.title: Great Shorts for the Court, but Could Use a Few Tweaks
customer_reviews.text: I’ve been playing basketball for a long time, and finding the right pair of shorts that are comfortable and functional can be a bit of a challenge. After hearing some good things about these basketball shorts, I decided to give them a try. Here’s what I’ve found after wearing them for a few days.Comfort and Fit:The first thing I noticed when I put these shorts on was how lightweight they are. They don’t feel bulky at all, which is really important when you’re running up and down the court. The material feels breathable, and it’s great for wicking away sweat. Even after a really intense game, I didn’t feel like I was carrying around a bunch of soaked fabric.As for the fit, they run true to size. I’m 6'0 and I went with a large, and they fit perfectly. Not too tight around the waist or thighs, but not baggy either. The waistband has a nice elastic feel that keeps them in place without feeling constricting. I’ve worn them through a few pick-up games, and I didn’t have to keep adjusting them, which is always a plus.Performance on the Court:When I’m playing, I need something that won’t restrict my movement, and these shorts do a great job. Whether I’m driving to the basket, playing defense, or just shooting around, the shorts don’t ride up or get in the way. The length is perfect, hitting just above the knee, which gives me plenty of mobility without feeling like I’m showing too much leg. The side slits at the bottom help with flexibility, allowing for more freedom when I’m making quick moves or pivots.They also do a good job of keeping me cool. I’m someone who sweats a lot when I play, and I was happy to find that the material breathes really well, helping to keep me comfortable during longer sessions. I didn’t notice any chafing or discomfort around the thighs, even after a few hours of wear.Durability:After using them regularly for a few weeks, I’m happy to say they’ve held up really well. I’ve washed them several times, and they’ve kept their shape, with no signs of wear or fraying. The stitching is solid, and the fabric hasn’t pilled or lost its stretch. I’m usually pretty rough on my basketball gear, so the fact that these shorts still look and feel brand new is a big plus.Aesthetics:These shorts have a simple, clean design. I got the black pair, which has a subtle logo on the side. I like the minimalist look; it’s not too flashy but still looks good. They come in a variety of colors, so you can easily find something that matches your style or team colors. The overall design is modern, and they fit the aesthetic I like when I’m on the court.The Downsides:One minor downside is that while the shorts are very comfortable, they could use a little more storage. There are no pockets, which is fine for playing, but it would be nice to have a small, hidden pocket for things like keys or a phone if you’re wearing them outside of practice. It’s not a huge issue for me because I mainly wear them just to play, but if you like having a pocket option, these shorts don’t offer that.Also, the fabric is super breathable, which is great for playing, but I noticed that in colder weather, they don’t offer much warmth. If you’re playing outside in cooler temperatures, you might need to layer up underneath or wear something else on top. But, for hot weather or indoor games, these shorts are perfect.Conclusion:Overall, I’m really happy with these basketball shorts. They’re comfortable, breathable, and perform well on the court. The fit is spot on, and they’re durable enough to handle regular use. If you’re looking for a pair of shorts to wear during your basketball games or practices, I’d definitely recommend these. However, if you need pockets or play in colder conditions, this might not be your best bet.Would I recommend them? Absolutely! They’re a solid choice for anyone who needs a functional, lightweight pair of basketball shorts.

customer_reviews.text: What I like:- light weight shorts, perfect for hot weatherWhat I don't like:- Dated polyester shorts style- Shallow pockets with no zip or button to secure phone or wallet- Minimalist construction, no lining, wicking waistband, pocket support, etc.I was looking for a pair of summer shorts to help keep me cool in the Florida heat. These Adidas Adi Advantage shorts looked ideal, a sports brand, designed for outdoor activities, what could go wrong?Out the package I wasn't impressed by the fabric. It is light weight, and quick drying, but it has the texture and appearance of polyester suit pants. This impression wasn't helped by the traditional styling which meant that when I tried them on my wife's first comment was that I looked like I'd borrowed my almost eighty year old father-in-laws old shorts. This isn't a youthful, active design.Wearing them I found the cut straight and baggy rather than slim and fitted. The waistband lacks a wicking/gripping liner, so unless they are a perfect fit or tightly belted they tend to ride down. The pockets are thin for breathability, and also relatively shallow becoming bulky rapidly with a wallet, handkerchief and keys. The back pockets also lack any zip or button security, so a phone or wallet easily bounces about and can fall out at anything more than a slow pace. Not ideal when I spend a lot of time chasing after my four year old kid!Overall, they are shorts, they do the job if they are your kind of thing, but for me I found the style and finish far below my expectations. A disappointing 3 out of 5 stars.

customer_reviews.title: Nice Shorts! Where's the Golf?
customer_reviews.text: I'm 6'0 tall and weigh about 200. I normally wear 36 waist and ordered 36 with these. Surprisingly they are a bit lose! I had a little thrill when faced with the possibility that I've trimmed down, but unfortunately, all my other 36's still feel the same as they did. I guess I have to conclude my pair of these adidas shorts run big.They are very nice shorts. The three stripes above the rear pocket and the adidas logo below the left front pocket are both subtle blue-on-blue, so these don't scream golf shorts or athletic shorts. But they are just four-pocket shorts.They stretch quite a bit, and they look good, and I'm certain that the material will breath and perform well, but there is nothing else about these shorts that makes them golf shorts and therefor command the premium price for golf wear. There is no special rear pocket for your score book, no secret tee-pocket, and they don't even have gripper material on the inside waistband to help keep your golf shirt tucked in.Again, nice shorts, but where's the golf? At a list price of $60, it would be nice to have some features that make these adidas golf shorts, and not just adidas shorts.

customer_reviews.title: Buying these because it's a Lululemon dupe? I ordered both. Here are my thoughts...
customer_reviews.text: These are commonly referred to as a dupe of the much more expensive Lululemon shorts. I needed athletic shorts and ordered both at the same time with a 5-inch inseam and linerless to see how close they actually are. I like a good deal, but I am also quite picky about quality and longevity. I read many reviews before buying, and here is the review I wish I had read.So...Are these just as good as the expensive shorts for less than half the price?-Fit:The term dupe means the same exact cut as the original. So, are they a true dupe? They are close.I ordered the 5-inch inseam in the CRZ shorts, and it feels more like a 6-inch inseam, so I tend to roll the band, which makes them feel more like a 5-inch inseam. You can see this difference in the pictures I've provided. Overall, they fit true to size. I ordered a L in both brands, and they fit about the same, maybe with slightly more leg room in the CRZ shorts.-Feel:Many say they feel exactly like the LL shorts. I'm fairly picky and disagree.It's closer in fit than it is in feel. They are not as soft, though they still feel quite nice in their own way. This could be due to the LL shorts' material being brushed in production or the material composition. The LL pace breaker shorts use rayon, which is a more premium fabric than the spandex used in the CRZ shorts. CRZ's material is thinner than the LL pace breaker, which makes them feel flowy in comparison. I like how lightweight the CRZ shorts feel. It barely feels like you have anything on.-Finish:You mostly get what you pay for here, with a little caveat...The pockets on the CRZ shorts are much better at accommodating my larger iPhone 11 Pro Max. Very deep pockets. The zipper on the CRZ shorts does feel a bit thinner and not as high quality as the LL. The pace breaker zipper feels sturdier and glides open with ease. The zipper on the CRZ is not as smooth. Hardware like zippers, grommets, buttons, etc., are where some costs were cut.I was hesitant to order these with people complaining about the drawstring fraying from the metal end coming loose after washing. I followed the wash instructions using cold water and air drying. I did not have this problem. I'm inclined to believe it's user error, assuming the metal end was more likely to come loose with heat and friction. The LL shorts use a plastic branded drawstring end, and the CRZ shorts use metal. The metal feels more premium by far.The CRZ shorts have a silicone label at the hem, and the LL have a stiffer plastic label. Silicone labels tend to not hold up as well if they are heat pressed. The CRZ branding seems to hold up well after washes.The color of the CRZ shorts is fairly accurate to the images shown online. I ordered a pair of the Green Sage and Gull Grey.-Final Verdict:Will I be buying more CRZ shorts or more Lululemon? I will be buying more CRZ.With the CRZ shorts, you get a little more than you pay for, and with the Lululemon, I think you are paying more than what you actually get. Comparing these two isn't fair, and I think the CRZ are good in their own way. I will be buying more of whatever lasts longer ultimately and will update this review if anything changes.-TL;DR: Buy the CRZ because they are good in their own way and not because they are a dupe.

customer_reviews.title: Similar to chubbies everywear shorts!
customer_reviews.text: I'm writing this review for those of you wondering if these are similar to the chubbies everywear shorts. I'll do a more in depth comparison, but from a high level they are extremely similar! There are a couple differences between them highlighted below. I have also included several pictures with direct comparison to actual chubbies which are my favorite shorts that I've been wearing for the past year or so. I snagged these up on prime day looking for a much cheaper alternative to my favorite chubbies shorts. These are super close for a fraction of the price.Biggest differences; maamgic is slightly longer (more material) overall despite having a half inch shorter inseam. Maamgic has also added a couple features not on the chubbies; metal tips on the drawstring, small key ring/loop on the front right belt loop, an additional 'change' pocket sown into the front left pocket. Maamgic also uses 90% polyester and 10% spandex, where chubbies is 89% polyester and 11% elasthanne.Minor differences; I would also say the threads and seams are a little more noticeable and visible on the maamgic depending on the colorway you choose. They only have one color for the drawstrings of the maamgic, if that matters to you. The chubbies have a slightly softer feel to them and less shiny looking, this could be that I've washed and been wearing the chubbies for awhile where I just got the maamgic shorts. The maamgic comes with a small elastic cord attached to the rear zipper pocket. There is also a slightly different tint to the similar colors of each brand just based on the materials they use.Maamgic pros; price ($37 difference), slightly longer overall, added belt loop key ring, metal drawstrings tips, added 'change' pocket inside front pocket, great basic colorways.Chubbies pros; name brand, slighter higher build quality (threads, seams, material & zippers etc) and overall softer feel, cool names for, along with, more colorways and patterns, both 6 inch and 8 inch inseam options.So if you're looking for a much cheaper alternative to chubbies everywear shorts, this is it! I plan to buy several in the colorways I'm missing from chubbies. I can't comment on the long term use of the maamgic compared to chubbies but I hope they hold up and last just as long! Let me know if this helps or you have any questions!

customer_reviews.text: For the price, I was surprised how well the coat is made. The seams are done well with tight stitching, and the internal fabric is smooth and comfortable. The buttons are easy to snap open and closed, and though I would have preferred a zipper, it's really not needed.I had to exchange the large for an extra large. The large was close, but the chest was just a little tight. I'm 5' 11 200 lbs, with low body fat. The large fit, but if I added a sweater underneath it was a little too tight. The extra large fits perfect, sleeves slightly long which I like. I'm glad I upped the size.

customer_reviews.title: Warm Jacket
customer_reviews.text: Warm Jacket. My husband loves the jacket and it is a great fit. Well made and looks great on him. Bought it more for working out side in the elements.

customer_reviews.title: I love it! Just a couple of small issues..
customer_reviews.text: I really like the fit and feel of this coat. It is very cozy and allows for good movement and layered clothing under it. I’m 5-10”, 215 lbs, somewhat broad shoulders and dad-bod belly. I ordered an XXL and I’m glad I did. I would much rather have a slightly large coat than one which binds in any way. The sleeves are about 1.5” too long without adjustment, but again, better than too short. I like the length as well, how it falls lower on hips at about the length of an untucked shirt. This coat (I selected black) is very stylish as well as warm, without having to be puffy. I like that it does not have a hood also. I’m not sure if it would be the best outdoor work jacket in frigid temps, but that’s probably not what most guys would expect in this one. It simply feels great on my body and looks dressy enough for date nights, etc. I don’t mind that it has snap buttons instead of a zipper. This detail kind of makes it a sharper looking coat, in fact. I usually leave coats open in front anyway, unless it’s exceptionally  cold out.A couple of things could improve this garment. The inside pocket (with Velcro closure) should be deeper to accommodate a cell phone better. Come on, everyone carries a phone and this detail would go a long way. Secondly, who thought the “Fashion Sport” patch on the sleeve would appeal to anyone? The leather-look patch itself looks okay, but put a duck or something generic on it. At least it’s not so glaring as to be a deal breaker. I can live with it.In closing, I’ll just say if you are a husky guy with a bit of a ponch belly, about 220-260 lbs, don’t have very short arms, and like freedom of movement, I believe you’ll like the XXL size. $70 seems fair for this nice coat.

customer_reviews.title: Cool jacket

customer_reviews.title: A Stylish Winter Jacket
customer_reviews.text: I love this jacket, and it is great for a mid winter temperatures.  I wore it when it was 26 degrees F, and I was quite comfortable.  I'm a tall female and the sleeves and length of the coat were perfect.  I like having snaps as opposed to a zipper too.  It is a sturdy coat.

customer_reviews.title: Great winter Jacket
customer_reviews.text: I was skeptical on the price but needed a new winter jacket as I recently relocated from Florida to Northern Texas and we get weather in the low teens during the winter months. This jacket is warm, first time I wore it, was 17 degrees outside and all I had underneath was a long sleeve shirt I wasn’t bothered by the cold at all. I notice a lot of people say buy a size up I got a medium I’m 6 foot about 175 lbs and it fit great. My only thing is engraving things like “fashion” on the buttons and the “fashion, sport” leather badge on the left sleeve are a little tacky, (I actually took the badge on the sleeve off with a needle and small knife), but for the money this is a great jacket that seems durable, fits to size and will keep you plenty warm in at least the weather conditions that I have explained.

customer_reviews.title: Nice Jacket
customer_reviews.text: This jacket was just as expected. Nice look and feel. Very good quality. The fit is good, but a little on the smaller side of the size. Still a 5 star item!

customer_reviews.title: Didn't get fleeced on this buy
customer_reviews.text: This coat arrived today. I was concerned about the size and the chart provided just didn't make any sense to me.  I normally wear a large so I wound up buying a large although the chart said I needed an extra large.  When I looked at the label inside coat the tag shows L for US and L for EU and XL for JP and XXL for CN.  So that solved the mystery. The coat is very well made and I like the snaps. The fleece lining is nice but not really fleece.  Didn't expect real fleece for this price but I do like the price.xx

customer_reviews.title: Great coat for cold weather
customer_reviews.text: My grandson picked this coat out for this year's season.  I like the looks, the specs looked good and they were on sale for a decent price so I bought one for myself as well.I am very happy with them.  Its heavy but not so heavy to uncomfortable.  We have not hit extreme cold yet but we have had some very cold days and have hit some cold days with some high winds putting the wind chill in the teens even flirting with single digit wind chills and this coat was great.  I was really impressed with how well this coat handles the wind.  It does not have a hood, but I did not really want one.  I am confident with this coat going deeper into harsher parts of a mid-west winter.  Its just big enough for me that if I need to layer a little bit in an Artic blast it will still be comfortable.  It does not have a hood which I did not want one.  I use an insulated gator and a good with hat and when it's really bad one of my layers will have a hood that I can pull over those for a little extra wind protection.  Just don't turn the heat up too high in the car or you will be pulling over to take it off LOL.  Only negative I have is that it says not to tumble dry on any level when you wash it and you can't dry clean it.  So, if you wash it be sure you are not going to need it for at least 2 days.

customer_reviews.title: Survived European Backpack Trip
customer_reviews.text: I bought this to take on a trip through the UK, France, and Italy. The jacket I purchased is yellow. I wanted something that would be adequately warm on a cool spring day so I wouldn’t have to bring another sweatshirt or have to pack long sleeve shirts. I also wanted something that folded up very small as I was only taking a backpack for 10 days. This jacket fit the bill perfectly. It comes with a bag which will compress the jacket down to about the size of a smaller shoe, but the way I found best to pack it was to fold it into quarters, flat, and put it on top of my clothes in my backpack. The jacket would compress almost completely flat, adding almost no bulk to my bag. It was like a magic trick how small it became. When I wanted to have it handy, but did not want to carry it, I would stick it through the handle of my backpack, pulling it halfway through, and it would stay there securely when I put my bag into overhead luggage storage on the Italo and Eurostar, making to easy to grab if I became cold.  There were some cold and very windy evenings and nights when we were in London and Paris (50 degrees F, with a strong breeze coming off the Thames and Seine) and this jacket kept me warm with just a t-shirt on underneath. I encountered a brief rain shower on the Path of the Gods and stayed dry and the jacket dried pretty quickly. I can’t speak to how well it would perform in a heavy downpour as that was the only rain I experienced during my trip. Overall, this jacket was perfect for me and at the price point, I was not going to be upset if it got lost, stolen, or ruined. After being stuffed in my bag over and over and shoved into overhead storage, the jacket still looks brand new. Not to mention it looked stylish in all of the photos my wife and I took! I am 6’6” and weigh about 190lbs and I bought a large. It fit well without a lot of extra bulk and the sleeves were long enough for my wingspan. 10/10, would recommend!

customer_reviews.title: Good cheaper alternative but not for heavy use
customer_reviews.text: I bought for the purpose of travel and outdoor use in those times where temps can change drastically from 70F in the morning down to 40F at night.I got this on sale for $20 which was a far cry from $60-120 asking price of other packable down jackets. For the price, it's much warmer than I thought and has well thought out features. So far I've worn this in 42F weather, coldest and just going on a walk I was breaking a bit of a sweat with it half zipped. It has 2 exterior pockets and 2 internal pockets. Personally I wouldn't put too much in these, as I can really feel the thing stretch and drag down. Just gloves, hat, phone etc. should be fine, nothing like a can of soda or something. Water resistance is what you expect for thin nylon stuff, a few drops is fine,  actual rain, get an umbrella or an actual waterproof layer. It's also pretty windproof, took it out in the aftermath of a pseudo hurricane and didn't feel the wind.It packs down pretty well into a 6 inch long 3 inch or so bundle but nothing like the high tech hiking stuff, I just wish there was a shorter loop so I can carabiner it to my pack easier but seems like it was intended to be carried like an umbrella. Also wish it packed into itself rather than have a bag which may get lost one day.  The material imo isn't very durable, I have no rips yet, but I'm not confident and think if I rub on something the wrong way it's going to tear. The stitching seems fine so far, and doesn't seem to be leaking filler yet.Sizing wise, I have a 45 chest and usually wear XL, but this is kinda big even for an XL, maybe because they were antiicpating you layer something like a thick sweater underneath. It is also a bit long for my torso, about 2-3 inches more than I need to sit at my waist. I have 23 sleeves and that fits perfect.I don't expect this to last a long time, but it's useful for the time I'll have it.12/28 edit:So I just used this exactly for what I bought it for because of the huge winter storm that swept across the north and east coast US. Temps went from nearly 60 degrees in daytime all the way down to 23 by late afternooon with extremely high winds that were throwing doors around and knocked some street signs off their mounts, and it was perfect. I just had a t-shirt underneath and on top of this was a gymax waterproof windproof jacket. Again my only complain might be if the material doesn't last and it's a bit long.

customer_reviews.title: Fits perfectly.
customer_reviews.text: I like the style and the soft feel. It's very warm for It's light weight. I've wished it and it didn't shrink. I would recommend this product.

customer_reviews.title: Great product
customer_reviews.text: It’s exactly as described. Lightweight, packable jacket. Comes with compression sack. Where I live it’s common for the temperature to be below freezing most of the winter and I use this coat the entire winter. I wouldn’t sit outside with it being that cold but as long as you’re active you’ll be warm. It holds your body heat really well when you’re active.  It sheds water and snow pretty good and blocks a lot of wind. The turtle neck/neck warmer is a really nice feature. The pockets are nice and roomy. Despite it being a cheaper alternative to more expensive versions/brands of similar coats it’s actually held up pretty good so far. The color was spot on to the example provided.

customer_reviews.title: Amazingly warm, lightweight, and so very useful.
customer_reviews.text: I have just gotten back from my trip to Japan in winter.  In my time there I am amazed by how often I used this jacket and how wonderful it was.First off it is surprisingly warm for the size.  I have a large REI travel jacket that is waterproof.  I noticed that when wearing that travel jacket I was cold!  I thought that the warmth of the travel jacket would have been equivalent to this puffer jacket, and I was very wrong.  It is very warm for it's size.It is very packable.  I often times packed it in the little duffle pouch, and pulled it out at evenings when it became cold.  It made all the difference, and kept me nice and warm.  It is part of a layering system and worked very well (Heat tech top and botton, jeans, a sweater, scarf, hat, and this puffer jacket).It was not exactly trendy, but did not look out of place in Tokyo.  Many many puffer jackets were on the streets, and it blended right in.  It was probably the single most useful purchase I made for the trip.  I wholly recommend this jacket.

customer_reviews.text: I spent a lot of time trying to figure out what size to order and I ended up going with the large tall. It fits extremely well. I have plenty of length in the sleeves, and plenty of room to layer a hoodie underneath if I need to, however this thing has been keeping me warm in 20-30° weather so far.The quality of the jacket is extremely nice, it has thick fabric and a nice hood. The only reason I am giving it 4 stars is because the zipper is not nearly as nice as one of my older carhartt jackets that I have. It is much smaller and does not feel as strong.Overall, I am loving the jacket after a few weeks of daily wear.

customer_reviews.title: Perfect Fit, Great Jacket.
customer_reviews.text: I was conflicted between the small and medium size, but I took a chance on the small, even know I normally wear mediums in hoodies and other jackets.I based my size off of a Wrangler work jacket I recieved last year for Christmas that was a size medium. Unfortunately, that jacket was a bit too big, for the sleeves went far past my wrists and the shoulder seams went too far past the end of my shoulder. It felt too bulky as well.So for this Carharrt I took a chance on the size small and didn't regret it. It fit perfect; the shoulder seams lined up and the sleeves covered my wrists perfectly. The length was good as well without it extending too low below my hips. I was even able to wear my favorite hoodie underneath it without the jacket feeling constrained and arm movement still feeling spacious.Keep in mind I have a relatively small frame, anyway so your mileage may vary.I asked my dad to try the jacket on, who is an inch shorter than me and has a more athletic build with slightly bigger shoulders, and it fit him perfect as well.The jacket itself feels high quality and will definitely hold up to some wear and the sherpa will definitely keep you warm. It's now probably the best jacket I've ever owned with plenty of pockets and a lightweight feel to the overall coat.Highly recommend if your considering it, for it is a solid alternative if the Detroit jacket lacks too little features for you.

customer_reviews.title: Sleeve cuffs WAY too tight!
customer_reviews.text: **UPDATE: I returned the L/Tall via UPS drop off, cost me $8 for them to box it up (lesson learned). I now have an XL/Tall and thankfully have slightly more room for my wrists in the cuff area, still very tight in the bottom part of sleeves but at least it will fit over my gloves! This would be my favorite jacket if the cuffs were not so tight/ if Carhartt used the same larger zipper from the older jackets (small zipper will be a pain to zip in the cold for sure, as other reviewers have rightly mentioned)/ Also the hand pockets are small... so I changed my rating from 3 stars to 4. If Carhartt fixed these 3 issues, then this would easily be my favorite jacket!-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------I'm 6'3 and 230 lbs.,was in great shape back in the day (Lifted weights/ Army lean an' mean), but now I look like a weasel that's preggers... So anyways, this new Large/ Tall sized jacket fits tighter in the chest area than my old Carhartt Large/ Regular (old Carhartt was a cheaper hooded style/ basic model). The sleeves are tighter compared to the old style (maybe because of Sherpa lining?), but the BIG reason I am leaving this review and returning this product for an XL/ Tall is because the sleeve cuffs are SOOO tight!! Even the outer sleeve around the stretchy cuff is crazy tight, so no way to pull my sweatshirt sleeves through the jacket cuffs and absolutely no way for me to tuck my long wool gloves inside the cuffs.This particular jacket was made in Indonesia. I know that the same model of clothing made in different countries will vary slightly (goes for all brands), but I am not sure if it is a quality control issue or if this new upgraded jacket is sized differently compared to the old base Carhartt model.Another con is that the zipper is smaller, as others have mentioned.Pros: this jacket feels warmer than my old basic model, arm movement will be better (in larger size, lol). I LOVE the Sherpa lining! Also, despite having a smaller zipper, I absolutely love the snap-over buttons! It is absolutely worth paying more for the upgraded buttons and lining!I hate to leave less than stellar review, but I will update it after I exchange this jacket for a larger one... If it is a quick worry-free exchange, then I will up the stars. If not, well... ITS COLD AND I NEED A JACKET NOW!!

customer_reviews.text: I was getting ready to take a trip to England, Scotland, and Ireland, and needed a jacket that would handle temps between upper 40's and lower 60's (October and November) with occasional rain.  This jacket handled all aspects admirably.  Using their sizing chart, size was perfect.  Jacket has a lot going for it, especially from a travel pespective:  It is easy to layer clothing underneath it, pockets are warm and lined, and something I found expecially helpful, was that the interior pocket is particularly deep.  Was great for gloves, paper items, etc. with no doubts about them staying in place.Coat is also excellent for when you have to change temps, such as you are going inside but still need to wear your coat.  It is light enough that it doesn't get in the way and you don't overheat with it on.  Bonus for the jacket was that it folds up well so that I could put it under the straps of my travel backpack and it would still fit inside the overhead bin.Got caught in the rain a couple of times (no surprise there) and it handled the rain extremely well, shedding the rain quickly and also drying quickly.Only minor negative (and it didn't impact me, but it might some) is that the zipper on the small pocket on the left sleeve (used for keys, etc.) had a habit of sliding open.  Again, no problem for me since I was not storing anything in there, but something to be aware of.All in all, an excellent purchase.  Worth the money.

customer_reviews.title: Almost a perfect fit
customer_reviews.text: I bought a few similar jackets from different manufacturers and the plan was to keep the one that fit the best. This one came in second place, and I had to return it because another one fit me a little better. I ordered the small, and I am 5'6 tall and 150 lbs with short limbs and a wide frame. Nothing fits me well, so I usually have to settle for something that is close but not perfect. This jacket fit perfectly, but the sleeves and overall length were just a little bit longer than a competitor. I honestly would have kept this jacket if I had not tried the competitor's, because the extra length was negligible and comfortable. Generally speaking, this jacket style runs a little long in the sleeves for people like me with short arms. Then, if you buy a size extra-small (usually not available), it's too tight or too short in the overall length. This is a nice, well-constructed, lightweight jacket that feels warm. It's much lighter than a parka but it seems like it will work for cold and wet weather around 40-45 F. The hood also fits well without a hat and it seems like a very functional go-to jacket for cold rainy weather. The wrist elastic could be a little tighter in my opinion, but it's basically snug around the wrist. You can probably put a few stitches in the material and make it tighter with some clever sewing.

customer_reviews.title: Beautiful fleece lined western jacket or shacket as they call it.
customer_reviews.text: So, this is designed to be worn as either a jacket or a shirt, allowing you to layer it in and wear it on cold blustery days.I am 6' 1 tall with an athletic build and the large was quite big.  I know it's to allow for a shirt underneath to be worn as a jacket, but it was just too big for me.  I returned it and ordered the medium which gives it a tailored look.I plan to wear it, here in Denver as a cold weather jacket and then as a shirt in the spring and summer.  It's really a great concept and allows for year-round wear (Denver is actually a very temperate climate, but plan accordingly depending on where you live).I got the brown with the plaid inner shell and it looks great.  This is a cotton/polyester blend with approximately 65/35 cotton to polyester respectively.I've ordered many, many shirts and the blend is the way to go in all cases.  I know everyone says cotton, but blends give you so much more in durability, comfort, moisture wicking properties, and bright colors.  I never by 100 percent of x in any shirt, it's always a blend.This looks great with jeans as casual wear; you can't go wrong and there is a wide selection or product with Legendary Whitetails store.Be careful on the care instructions as the tag states this may bleed if washed with white colors in warm to hot water.  It's best to do the first wash by itself and then wax the shirt with a water repellant wax to waterproof it.

customer_reviews.title: Durable, Attractive, Multi-Functional Shirt/Jacket

They were a big hit at our family Christmas party. The only complaint I overheard came from the boys wanting more of them.This particular shirt/jacket is definitely more of a jacket than a shirt. I mentioned that I ordered several different colors and styles of this brand. Fortunately, the son who attends college in Boulder ended up with this one. All of the other Legendary Whitetails Shirt/Jackets I ordered were more on the shirt side of a shirt/jacket. This worked out well for us because we live in Louisiana, my other son is in Pharmacy school in the deep south, and my two nephews live in Texas.This Shirt/Jacket is exceptionally comfortable and is good for colder weather. It's not clothing you would want to keep on while inside.Regarding sizing, my son said it is true to size. He is a true Medium in nearly everything I purchase. He's 20 years old, 5'10 or maybe 5'll, and about 160 pounds. He works out and is fit, but has broad shoulders. I bought a size Medium for my husband as well. He is 170, 5'10. My other son is about the same height and weight.They can easily wear a shirt, sweatshirt, hoodie, or turtleneck beneath the shirt/jacket. I suggest ordering your normal size unless you like your jackets to fit baggy or you are larger in the stomach area. If you live in the north or midwest and plan on layering more than one article of clothing under the shirt/jacket, you may want to consider the bigger size.This shirt/jacket is a remarkable deal for the price. Everyone who received one as a gift from me has worn theirs multiple times. The jackets look better now -- with that worn-in look. It keeps the bitter cold of Michigan from biting and protects from harsh wind. The shirt/Jacket has several interior and exterior pockets.I can tell when someone genuinely likes a gift and this topped our family Christmas bestseller list and has already been added to the repeat performer list for 2022.If you're looking for a heavier shirt/jacket for colder months, one that you can layer or wear over a sweatshirt or hoodie, this is for you. If you are looking for a lighter-weight shirt/jacket that you can leave on indoors then I would try one of Legendary Whitetails many other shirt/jacket options.Overall, this is a fabulous product. It outperforms competitors in value, purpose, and appearance. That’s a winner in my opinion

customer_reviews.title: Bought twice, would buy again
customer_reviews.text: I bought this jacket first five years ago and ordered a large, which was my standard size at the time. What I got back then was a quality jacket but one that could be a bit uncomfortable to wear given that the arms were insulated with a weird material and it also ran quite small. Still, I rather liked it and thought it looked really nice, so I wore it until I put on some weight and outgrew it.Eventually ordered a new one in XXL, which is what I order in jackets now because I like them to be a little loose and baggy when I'm at work, my t-shirt size is XL. New version of the jacket is of even higher quality. The material it's made of still feels strong but is very very smooth almost like suede, and the arm insultation is vastly better. The XXL feels like it ran a little big this time, as it's quite loose on me now, moreso than other jackets I order in that size, but for me this is fine. I could easily wear a big sweater or hoodie with it in cold weather and still fit comfortably. If you're unsure, I would say you would likely be safe ordering this in your usual size even if you like things to hang a little looser. I bought the brown/'tobacco' color and it is an extremely attractive jacket I feel like I could wear a lot of places from my messy custodial job to mountain hiking to dinner at like a sit down sushi place. It's of a quality and appearance that I feel you could wear this on a date or a night out and you would look quite nice. The buttons look quite nice and are kind of a weathered brass look. Previous jacket had a problem with the wrist buttons coming undone constantly, seems to be fixed in this one. The flannel insulation is not thick and I would consider this more of a spring/fall jacket, but I could easily layer it if the temperatures dropped.

customer_reviews.title: Rugged, good look and nice fit, but should you go down a size?  A couple caveats. . .
customer_reviews.text: The short answer to if you should go down from your typical size or not: yes, you probably should; that is, if you only plan on wearing this shirt jacket without layering.  However, if you plan on wearing this with a bulker hoodie or something similar underneath OR you have a larger stomach, then probably not.  If you are interested in more specifics, please continue reading. . .I wanted a heavier shirt jacket that I could wear over a light to medium-weight hoodie for the upcoming colder months.  I normally take an XL or a L depending on the brand, and if I plan on layering or not.  I have an athletic build (larger shoulders and chest and smaller waist), and, usually, when I plan on layering with a hoodie, I need an XL; but being that many said this runs large, I opted for a L.  Glad I did. . .The large fits well over my medium-weight hoodie, had just enough room for movement where I didn't feel like it was too tight and restricting.  It also fit well enough without the hoodie, not too loose and baggy.  If I would have gotten an XL as I normally would, then the fit would have been a little too loose for my liking, especially while wearing the jacket without layering.  Personally, I prefer a little a snugger fit since it holds in body heat better when working in below freezing temps; but my preference for a slightly snugger fit may not be pleasurable for you.  For reference, I am between 5'11 and 6 feet tall, weigh 200 lbs., have 53.5 inch shoulders, 47 inch chest and 33 inch waist (shoulders, chest and waist measured in circumference).If you are someone who likes a much looser fit and/or has a larger midsection, I would recommend getting your usual size -- at least.  This shirt jacket is more streamlined in the body than what many other shirt jackets are, so if you have a larger belly and went a size down, this shirt jacket will most likely be a bit too tight for you.  This I know:After I purchasing mine and wearing it a bit, I bought another one for my stepfather.  Unlike me, he has smaller shoulders. . .and a fairly large midsection.  He normally takes a L for his jackets, but since this shirt jacket runs a little large, I opted for a M.  It didn't fit.  It was OK for him in the shoulders, but the jacket wouldn't button over his larger belly.  I returned it and got a large for him, which then did fit over his larger midsection, but barely.This shirt jacket does have side pockets and one pocket inside up by the chest area for a smart phone, wallet or whatever.  One thing I should say about the side pockets is that they are awkwardly placed.  The manufacturer put the side pockets right on the seams where the front and back parts of the shirt jacket are sewn together, and so the pockets are a bit farther back from where typical side pockets would be -- from my experience anyway.  If you want to use them to warm your hands, you better have flexible shoulders.Also about the pockets. . .not the side ones, but the inside pocket up by the chest: Some people have commented that the Velcro is overly strong and thus there are some concerns of tearing the inner liner when pulling open the pocket.  Yes, it is strong, like most new Velcro is, but. . .if you grab each part of the Velcro with your hands and close and open it a couple of hundred times (this may sound like a lot work, but I did so in only a couple of minutes), the Velcro will loosen up. . .and considerably.The thing that I am the most disappointed with is the snap buttons: They are very weak.  The snap buttons are metal and look nice and sturdy, but several of them would not stay snapped together very well.  They would pop open with minimal effort, like bending over, for example. Thankfully, though, not all of them are so exceptionally wimpy -- just a few of them.  So for most part, the shirt jacket stayed partially buttoned.In all, this is a very nice looking, feeling and sturdy shirt jacket which is quite warm when worn with a hoodie.  It does a good job keeping out the wind and it appears to shed some water as well.  It also goes on and off very easily because of the inner nylon-lined sleeves. But because of the weakness of some of the snap buttons and the extreme side placement of the side pockets, I cannot give this more than four stars.*Update*I've been wearing this shirt jacket for approximately 18 months now, during Fall and Winter mostly, and it has held up well.  It has endured a lot of abuse during that time, and it still looks good -- no tears, no scratches and no coming undone at the seams.  But. . .as I stated before, those darn snap buttons sure could be a lot stronger.  Many times while I was out doing something strenuous, like cutting brush or shoveling a lot of snow, I looked down and saw the bottom half of the jacket unbuttoned.  I don't know if I got a bad batch of buttons, or if the rest of these shirt jackets are this way.  It is a minor complaint, but it does get a little annoying when working hard and then constantly having to rebutton the jacket.And as for how warm it is during winter. . .I'm impressed.  With the configuration of clothing I have shown in my photos (tee-shirt, long sleeve denim shirt, medium weight hoodie and this jacket) , I've been good in -25 to -30 temperatures (and that is not including the wind chill), that is, as long as I stay active.  My face and hands were another matter, though. . .I would like to be able upgrade my rating for this jacket, for the overall quality of this shirt jacket is high and it is also very warm.  But the weakness of the snap buttons prevents me from rating it better than what I originally did.**Second update**Been two and a half years of wearing this jacket. . .and it is still in excellent shape.  Even though I've put this shirt jacket though a lot of abuse (cutting, hauling and piling firewood, cutting multitudes of brush and many other outside jobs where I was crawling around in the dirt), the shell is still intact -- no tears or rips or seams coming undone.  The inside is fully intact as well.  Unfortunately, the metal snap buttons have weakened a bit more.  I recently took a photo of myself after I was done cutting down some balsam trees on my property.  You can get a better look at how the jacket looks in an outside environment.  And as testament to what I have been saying about the snap buttons, you can see that the lower half of the jacket is unbuttoned.  It is such a shame that these buttons are so weak, for it degrades the overall quality and appeal of this otherwise outstanding jacket.

customer_reviews.title: Good value, you get what you pay for
customer_reviews.text: I read the critical reviews, and still ordered it.  Amazon even warns that this particular item has a more-than-usual return rate.  I am keeping mine.  First is the material.  Polyester/Spandex could mean almost any thing; it is not Italian wool and I did not expect it to look like it was.  I have no idea how the material will hold up.  The size and styling is called slim fit which means it is not made for most American men.  I take a size 2 -- I am too short, too fat, too old.  Nothing off the rack is gonna fit me.  For pants I need a 40 inch waist and a 24 inch inseam.  I have a small chest with a big pot belly. I buy dress shirts at Macy's and expect to double the price when I add in the tailoring needed. This jacket was priced at about the same as a good weight pair of 501 jeans.  I was not expecting bespoke fit or construction.  The next up is the design.  It is called 'a blazer' .  For me that means patch pockets and contrasting metal buttons.  This jacket has neither.  The three sleeve buttons had sparse button hole stitching.  It was so fake that when I had the sleeves shortened, I had similar decorative stitching added to continue the joke.  It does not have the typical fake stitched button hole on the lapel that is convenient for wearing decorative or identifying pins. The pockets are slit with flaps.  It may not be clear from the pictures, but there are two inner pockets and the jacket is fully lined.  Yes it is very light weight.  But now, even in the heart of winter, I rarely will be wanting to wear my real bespoke Shetland Wool tweed sport coat.  Everywhere is heated much warmer now.  Also, it has center vent, not mentioned.  That is important for me because the usual side vents show off my big butt.I wanted a light weight jacket that looked better than a zippered hoody, for casual wear -- unbuttoned -- year round.  I think this will do me just fine.

customer_reviews.title: Be careful of inaccurate reviews of this good jacket

The zipper mechanism is on the left hand side instead of the right hand side which really doesn't matter to me it functions I am not concerned with zipper etiquette.Some people are led to believe that this is a woman's jacket because the zipper is on the left, well I've seen soft shell jackets for women as I bought some for my partner and they are usually pleated around the upper chest and armpit area to allow room for breasts. This jacket is not pleated in such a way so I would say that's wrong.Although women can wear the jacket I'm just saying it does not possess that pleat that allows extra room for lady partsI would love if this had an attachable Hood as it does not the hood is permanently attached but can be rolled away although I'm not sure why you would want to anyway but you can you have options.That does not detract from the quality of the jacket in any way as it is not stated as having a removable Hood so there's no reason to deduct a star for that.This jacket will keep you warm it will keep you protected and it looks good. It's true to size as far as I can say and the material is satisfactory.It does have pull cords within to adjust the fit of the jacket as well as the hood and in other reviews I have taken note that they report their jacket not having retention clasps for the chords but mine does.Again I don't know if they got it defective jacket or if this jacket has changed and the company has fixed the issues.
