customer_reviews.title: It's Weird.......but stood up to the test
customer_reviews.text: I live in Montana and bought this for late fall thru early spring working outside. I have also used this for hiking during those times. I put this jacket through -20F to 45F in rain, snow, wet snowy rain, wind and sunshine. Bottom line is I liked it more than I didn't and for $40 I'm happy. BTW I bought the Army green version.If you are thinking about buying this, I feel like this is important to know:1 - It's a softshell outer jacket - Not a winter coat.  It is parka style meaning it comes down below the buttox and has 2 zippers on the front.2 - It's not waterproof - It is water repellant and did a good job in wet snow keeping me dry on a daily basis. It dried out fairly quicky when hung by a fire.3 - It's a really weird coat!PROS:Looks awesome!Lots of zippered pockets (which is also a con)Sleeve length was perfect and the bottom didn't rise up above my waist when reaching overhead.Loved the construction of the hood with the reinforced bill and the adjustable straps for both the hood and bottom of the jacket.The armpit zippers is why I bought this in the first place!Very thin layer of fleece on the inside.Snowshoeing at -10F with a base layer and the arm pit zippers open, I was plenty warm! Which is what I was looking for in jacket.CONS:The fit was off for me. Not by a lot, just a really small portion that didn't warrant ordering a larger size because then it would be way to big. It was tight in the shoulders and arms were super tight.No way you are getting cell phone in any of those arm pockets.Zippers are not seam sealedNo stretch to the materialVelcro cuff tighteners - yeah.....I don't see that lasting in the rain for more than a couple years.Not for hunting - this is the noisiest jacket I own! It is loud when you move!If you wear a short sleeved shirt under the jacket you can feel the cold armpit zippers on your inner arm.WEIRD:The elbows or perhaps forearms have a reinforced outer layer. But it doesn't come to the elbows on me or completely cover my forearms (for when I am crawling I guess?)It has these 2 inner pockets? Or for some other purpose that I can't figure out because it is not sewn on the bottom (see pic) So it stores nothing.You have these random weird velcro patches on the bottom of the jacket and back of the hood that I have no idea what they are for.I am guessing the weird velcro pocket on the inside of the hood is for you to roll up the hood, but why would you?Zippered back pockets - I can't even reach them! Not even sure what the purpose of them being there is other than to transport gear which I wouldn't do because the coat is not fully waterproof. Might be good for storing some cans of beer though on a hike.Inner cinching strings for the hood run along the inner coat into the kangaroo pockets. Easy to get this caught or torn (see pics)The jacket is weird, but it has worked well so all is good.

customer_reviews.title: A good quality, long length basic raincoat
customer_reviews.text: This is a no frills rain coat that does what it should: keep the rain off. It's made of nylon-poly fabric with a rubber-like coating. It has a rain proof zipper along with a zipper-covering flap that fastens with metal snaps. The snaps are good quality that are easy to use and look like they'll last. There's a good size hood with a drawstring. There are two 6.5 by 7.5 pockets with flaps but no snaps. I'm 5' 9 and a medium fits me well. There is enough room for a bulky hoodie sweater.Overall, I gave this a rating of 4 stars. It didn't get the fifth star for several reasons. First of all, there are no vents, not in the arm pits, not along the upper back. The fabric is non breathing, so in warmer weather you're likely to get a bit sweaty if the coat's fully zipped. The pockets are simple patch pockets with no access to inside pockets. If you're in the rain digging for keys in your pants pockets you have to unzip or pull the coat up.  There are no cord locks on the hood drawstring. If you want to tighten the hood opening you'll have to tie a knot and then untie it when you want out of the coat. The zipper does not have the option to partially open from the bottom. If you have a longer stride you may find the zipped coat a bit constraining due to coat's length. To be fair, you could not use the zipper and depend on the top three or four snaps.Overall I like this raincoat. It's not perfect, but none of its shortcomings are showstoppers.

customer_reviews.title: Great Coat. Great Price.
customer_reviews.text: Extremely happy with my purchase. The coat looks great and looks of decent quality for the price. It's nice to be able to stay outside the $200-$400 higher side coat price range and get something that looks good and fashionable. I rotate clothes a lot, so having several winter coat options at more reasonable prices fits the bill perfectly, just as this coat does. And, at the price, if can get 1 or 1.5 seasons wear, I'm happy.As for coat fit, I'm 6'3, 34x34 pant, 15 1/2 neck, 36 sleeve, 40 chest, 175 lbs, more triangular build. The large fits a bit loose at top, but that's my issue as I prefer a bit tighter fitting clothing. So, not a manufacturer problem in my opinion as some online clothes can be. More so, I wouldn't downsize due to the sleeve length which was absolutely perfect. And, above all, the extra size accommodation at top, of course, is likely given to accommodate a suit/sport coat underneath. And, while peoples suit/sport coats length can vary, if my suit/sport coat is buttoned, this coat covers such an undercoat just fine. If the suit/sport coat is unbuttoned, that coat hangs a bit out from underneath from this coat. Not an issue. Just FYI. And, with my preference for likely wearing with just a sweater, this size will be great and as tailored to one as one can expect from ordering online.I ordered the coffee 01 color, and no disappointment there. What I saw in the pictures, is what I got. I was worried the blend might look a bit cheesy. But, no. Very refined looking and just the color I wanted.Some people said they didn't like the buttons, that they are maybe a bit flashy, i.e., not just solid color or standard brown/black. If you are way conservative in dressing, or need that, perhaps so. I get it. But, I think they are a nice accent. I worried a bit about that too. But, when I got the coat. Not a problem at all. Looks great and if a real concern I think the coat is worth it to have a tailor put on the buttons you want.Last, there seems to be a bit of confusion on the reviews as to whether its too short or that its more of a waist coat. Yes, this version is. For me, it fits more to my upper thigh, or right at mid-point on pants pockets. HOWEVER!!!, within the color options, different lengths are presented, so beware! And that is perhaps what people are noting. One color you like, might be a different coat style/length than another color you like. So, carefully read the description and look at the sleeve bottom to coat bottom ratio in the pictures for length approximation or read the size charts, which I think pretty accurately depict the difference.I picked up on this difference and decided to also order a longer length coat in another color by this manufacturer, in case the first didn't seem to fit as I wanted. I am keeping both! as these are really decent wardrobe additions and each of the lengths I thought I was picking is exactly what I got. One other point on some of the comments, this coat did come with a scarf. The other coat under this manufacturer that I got with the listing shown to come with a scarf, did not. So people have noted this. Perhaps true. But, in seeing that possibility ahead of time before ordering, I knew scarf or no scarf was not going to be a deal breaker at this price. Also, I believe some folk contacted the manufacturer and got the scarf separately. Again, not a deal breaker for my purpose.Anyhow, long review....but I was really impressed with the coat(s) from this brand/manufacturer. In buying 2 at still a fraction of a $400 single coat price, I can rotate and likely get better dress options and similar wear, and I will look for this seller's clothing in the future.

The other down side is that the right pocket had a giant hole in the bottom that fed into the insulation portion of the bottom of the jacket. The actual insulation is light and feels like pulled apart cotton balls (not a bad thing, just weird). I had to sew it up and now it feels weird because I'm horrible at sewing. I probably could have exchanged it...but I ordered it late into winter here and needed a new coat so I dealt with it.Otherwise, for this price this jacket was well worth it. I'm not sure I'd buy it again because the fit is a bit off. The arms are perfect length, it's just the chest that sits a bit tight. If you are more on the narrow side of chest size though, this could be perfect for you. If not for the massive hole in the pocket, I would have given this 4 stars because it really is a great value at this price point.

customer_reviews.text: This one just showed up. It used soft Amazon and manufacturer patching, so it was wrinkled to the point that it needed either an iron, or time in a dryer (which incidentally is against the instructions on the tag).Problem: Other reviewers have noticed the patches that are very carefully not shown in the Amazon photos. But when you're looking at the thing...yeah, they're there. Also they stick up enough that they may be a catch-and-tear issue. Mine actually showed up damaged with a tear along a long edge of the patch, showing the interior construction. Replacement is on the way, but the best-case scenario is that it'll be in good condition but with those two ridiculous patches. I may hit a local hobby shop for a #11 X-Acto knife to carefully remove them by cutting the stitches one-by-one. Time-consuming but worth it. It looks like one viewer above has already done just that.So, by all appearances, five stars for the coat itself. Fabric looks good, size is great, coat seems warm with fake fur lining around chest (not the sleeves), fake-fur-lined hood is removable (if a little ridiculously large (which may not be a bad idea if you're already wearing a stocking cap or a hoodie). But. Minus 2 points for REALLY trying to hide those patches in the product photos, plus the item showing up damaged.

customer_reviews.title: Warmth and wind resistance
customer_reviews.text: This is a great jacket for the price.  Zipper is sturdy and cuffs are snug to keep out the wind.  Calling it heavyweight is fine -- but it's not as bulky and heavy as my 23-year old parka (which is still in decent shape), for example.  So, I'd say it provides a lot of warmth for its weight.The handwarmer pockets are big enough for a heavy glove, and the interior pocket has a velcro closure to secure your phone or wallet.The hood is well shaped: it lays down nicely when not in use, and you can mold around your head -- I don't miss having a draw-cord.  It seems pretty secure in the wind as long as you angle it properly.  The fleece lining keeps my head warm when I'm not wearing a knit cap.Fit: I'm 42 chest, and I bought a medium.  I still have room to wear a heavy sweatshirt or sweater under this coat.  I have to say that in temperatures from the mid-20s to high 30s, I don't really need a heavy layer underneath.  Wind resistance is very good.Just started trying Amazon Essentials clothing in the last 8 months, and have been quite satisfied, so far.  This piece seems like another good value, as long as it proves to be durable.

customer_reviews.title: It's all in the details
customer_reviews.text: Me: 5'9, 230 lbs. Bought XXL, black. Fit as expected. Reasonably light in weight, not bulky. Could layer a hoodie under the jacket if desired. Arm length good for my 35 arms. Cuffs on sleeves for warmth. Hood: substantial, fleece lined, but no drawstring to tighten in the wind. No drawstring to tighten at the jacket's base either, which was just below my beltline, though little room for cold air to blow up & in given my 40 waist. Two medium sized lined outside diagonal pockets with easy-to-operate YKK zippers. One inside left lined breast pocket that was vertical in orientation with a 2cm Velcro strip closure - I'd have preferred a horizontal orientation so nothing drops out if the Velcro fails. Front closure also used same size YKK zipper as pockets. A flap with 5 snaps could be closed over the zipper for additional warmth. I like how the front zipper rises 2-3 up the neck like a scarf for additional warmth. Fabric sheds water effectively. Entire jacket is polyester/ polyester fiberfill. Machine wash cold, dark colors, delicate cycle - dry on low setting. NO dry cleaning. I have been pleased with my ability to move freely in the coat. I'm comfortable at 30*F, even when the wind chill is in the low 20's. Have not laundered yet - I'm hoping the fiberfill does not shift where I lose any insulating properties. Build quality seems good for a coat this reasonable in cost. Would recommend.

Although I do agree to a degree, the length is a bit short for my liking but isn't a deal breaker.I'm 5'7 with just a tad bit of a stomach (stuck on a temporary desk job) and I think the girth of this coat is just a tiny bit tight but again, not a deal breaker because of my poor choice of eating habit...lol. The breast pocket buttons are not very well stitched in and may fall off at some point in time as the stitching really is weak and not strong. In the pictures I posted, you can see the inside of my hand and outside showing the length is a good fit. Also I was able to take a rear picture showing the length of this coat from behind.The very last thing I was a bit disappointed in...the color. In the listing, the pictures show a crisp sharp image. I like my flannels and plaids a little big because I carry concealed and those are deciding factors for me in these types of clothing. But if I were to grade this on a 5-Star grading, I'd probably give it a 4.5 just because I was disappointed with the coloring being blurred but that isn't a deal breaker.After wearing this just around the house, I think maybe this probably would fall under a jacket as I am discovering this jacket is a bit thin. But it really is comfortable to wear.Hope this helps...Update: November 13, 2023...Ok so I finally got around to ordering the XL size and I got to admit, this fits waaaay better then the size Large which I did return. Again, this is probably not the kind of jacket/coat to wear out in the freezing cold.This is more or less the kind of jacket to wear during those chilly evenings or day. I'm from Northern Idaho and I am familiar with the harsh winters and some winters are worse then others.If you plan on just wearing this to the store, fine go for it but bring something else too just in case. customer_reviews.title: Cheap Quality, Runs Small In Legs
customer_reviews.text: I retired 20 years ago. I have ordered many, many sweat pants and athletic pants over the years. I wear this stuff on a daily basis. Here's my feedback and advice.1. First impression is they are way too thin. You can hold them up to a window and see light thru them. Think of these more as pajama bottoms and not sweats. You can wear them in public tho.2. They are indeed comfortable. The material is soft. It feels descent on the skin (most polyester does).3. The stitching is terrible. This is a manufacturing problem that should not exist. I don't see these lasting 20-30 wash cycles without falling apart.As a rule of thumb ALWAYS order sweats and athletic pants 3x your size. If you plan on being very active with them then consider up to 5x your size and have them hemmed. What you're looking for is air around the legs. That thermal barrier is where the comfort comes from. It's what keeps you warm. These are not blue jeans or suits, so shop for that air gap around the legs. Baggy is better! These are not baggy. Maybe the 5x would be appropriate for most of us. But having their length trimmed and hemming adds a level of concern that shouldn't exist.Outside of the above mentioned I would recommend one last thing. Try to find athletic pants that have a liner. Lined sweats / athletic legs are the most comfortable thing you will ever put on your body. You will never be more comfortable. And look for a thin cotton and polyester blend for the inner liner. These are super, super hard to find. But if you can find them, snag them. You'll thank me.

customer_reviews.title: A+ for comfort, not meant for warmth
customer_reviews.text: TL;DR - insanely comfortable pants well-suited to wear around the house and outdoors as long as it isn’t too cold; they are extremely thin and won’t offer much warmth but I cannot say anything negative about this purchase; worth buying a backup pair for when I wear the . . .  pants . . .off of these pants!One evening last month I put on a pair of warmup pants — THE warmup pants, I had no other — and realized they weren’t all that new when Pope JPII was alive, and the elasticity was gone completely, and there was too much pant material for my frame, and maybe I should retire these.They were fairly heavy, but I live in a sub-tropical climate and hardly ever need anything so heavy.So I bought these because they were rated well and inexpensive compared to other known brands and I was not going to be hassled by the thousands of off-brand options, all of which I regard as a gamble at best and a hassle at worstI am very pleased with my purchase. For context, I am 6’0”, between 160 and 165 lbs depending on the day, and could reasonably be described as long-legged but not drastically so.Size: I bought medium, and they fit me perfectly. Take my height and weight into account in deciding your size. They even might run a hair long, but that could be due to how they sit at my waist.Style: I wear these in and around the house, and need only impress my dog, so these were simple and basic enough that I didn't much care how they look, but the photos are accurate.Comfort: I have achieved maximum comfort permitted by natural pants law, and wear these at all times until I go out during the day, and from after I get home and dress down.Material: The material is very thin and lightweight. I don’t think I would want to be outdoors in temperatures below 60° F for long in these, but that’s not of much concern to me. If you have cooler temperatures often enough  and want something to wear outside, this is not the right option.If this description matches your need, you cannot go wrong with these!

customer_reviews.title: The Good The Bad The Ugly

THE BAD - While I love draw stings I don't love these drawstrings. What they do is take a length of string and bring the ends together in the back of the pants and sew the ends down. The problem is sometimes they don't get them sewed down very good at all. Some will come loose in the back and when it does it is almost impossible to get the string threaded back through the waist band. THE UGLY - While these are the most comfortable pants you will ever wear they are not durable. Granted the will NOT ball up but if you have to do anything where you are actually working they will wear, snag easily. These pants are very delicate and as long as you are doing no work they will be fine as long as the drawstrings stay sewed.

customer_reviews.text: In my household, we spend a LOT of time in a volleyball gym. My wife coaches and I sometimes assist and my 3 daughters all play very high level. If you spend anytime in a volleyball gym, at night, in the winter, you know that you might as well be playing outside. Same goes for tournament venues on those super nice Saturday pre-dawn mornings in the low desert. Long story short, I was sick and tired of freezing every time I attended a tournament, so I bought these PURE CHAMP jogger sweatpants and boy am I glad I did.Fist of all, they are warm. Like if the temps exceed 72, be ready to sweat. (Full Star)Second, they are comfortable. Soft and dare I say plush. I also really enjoy the zippered pockets to help secure small items like Air Pods. (2 stars)Third, they are well made. The seams are string, and the previously mentioned zippers are solid, I have no doubt these will last long enough to be worth their cost. (2 stars)LASTLY!!!!!  WATCH THE SIZING. In pants like this, I normally wear a large (36 waist, 32 inseam) and T, without looking at the sizing chart, ordered a set in my size. They fit great upon arrival, even after the first few washes if I tumble dried or air dried them. After 1 heated dry cycle....the pants are...more form fitting than desired. Yes, they have a high cotton content, yes it was my error, but they feel as if they have shrunk a full size and a half to two sizes.Anyways, I recommend sizing up from your norm and dry away. For this, I was going to deduct a star, but it was my ignorance that caused the pants to shrink and my inpatients that prevented me from reviewing the manufacturers sizing chart, so the product itself still gets all the stars.

customer_reviews.title: I liked the old model better, but these are okay.
customer_reviews.text: I cannot say anything is wrong with this item.  I just liked the old model that I bought a few years back.  The current models that I just bought are labeled h46110, h48429, 48431.  The models from three years ago that I still have are ei9759, ei9760 and ei9761.  I don't think that the old model is made any longer.The new ones are made from recycled material.  I have no idea if that matters in term of form or function.  All are 100% polyester.  (I don't think that you can see the model number except on the pants themselves and the packaging, but you can Google it and get accurate results.)I am tall and thin and found that the current version is slightly looser on me than the old one.  I wear a medium.  I bought them online, but I think that a small might be too tight.  The drawstrings are two separate strings like shoe laces, not one loop.They fit okay, but once again, just seemed slightly loose even when I tied the strings.  Still, they are wearable although I might look elsewhere in the future.  The length is good for me with running shoes on.  They come down around ankle.  (I wear prewashed 32x34 jeans which I put in the dryer which definitely shrink a bit despite being prewashed so I am probably closer to a 31x33.)I noticed no shrinkage after a few dry cycles or color running when washing in cold water, medium dryer, but I did wash them separately first to be safe.  The old model was also 100% polyester but seemed to shrink slightly for whatever reason.The stitching in the back is not as attractive in my mind compared to the old model, but I don't know if this matters, especially with darker colors.  It seems like they are constructed differently with an extra piece in the back.  In other words, instead of having one piece connected from the legs to the waist band, there seems to be an additional piece between,  You would never notice a problem if you didn't have the older version, and it certainly is not a reason not to buy them, but since I have the older model, it bothered me a bit.I think that most people would be happy for the price that I paid; but, as seems to happen with everything that I like in this world, they replace it with something that is acceptable but not as good.

customer_reviews.title: The Soft and Thin ADIDAS Track Pants
customer_reviews.text: Exactly what I wanted.  Been wearing these pants in one form or another for over 20 years.  They’re very comfortable.  These ones I got, are the softer material.  It’s not the plasticy nylon type material that wooshes between your thighs when you walk.  It’s the nice and soft variety.  I have had two thicknesses of these pants, these are the thinner material.  If you daily these like I do, then you will probably appreciate this review clearing up exactly what you can expect.On this occasion I got the XL Tall size.  The price was right, so I ordered several pairs in differing colors.  I’ve never tried the tall size.  As far as I can tell they’re roughly the same as standard XL, maybe a little tighter around the thighs.  The pairs I own I’ve had for awhile and maybe they’re stretched out, so maybe it’s the same, but these are definitely tighter around the thigh than the pairs I’ve had for years.  I have large thighs, if you don’t have large thighs, it won’t bother you.  It doesn’t bother me actually, but I can tell they’re a little tighter than normal.  Which is fine, it’s good to have a bit of variety and they’ll probably stretch the older they get.  I just hope they don’t shrink in the wash.  One thing unique about these pants is they typically do not shrink in the dryer.  So the tall aspect of the size, yes they are 2 inches, I believe, longer than your standard XL.  I already dragged the pant cuffs around on the carpet, it’s just a little more noticeable.I think you should be able to see in the pic I attached to my review the fabric of these pants to help aid you in determining what it is you’ll get.I hope that helped out one of my fellow ADIDAS track pants lovers out there.

customer_reviews.title: Review of 10 Pairs of Sweatpants
customer_reviews.text:
I waited almost a year to post this review to see if my initial conclusion was correct.  Essentially it was.  The bottom line is the Polo Ralph Lauren French Rib pants fit and feel the best of any pants.  Unfortunately, they’re expensive and not available on Amazon.  However, there are some pairs available on auction sites for reasonable prices. The next best is between the U.S. Polo Assn. Men's Fleece Cargo Pant and the Champion Men's Champion Eco Open Bottom Pant.  The problem with the U.S. Polo Assn. Men's Fleece Cargo is that they pill a lot and because they’re made of nylon they don’t breathe well if at all.  The problem with the Champion is they’re a bit long, a bit baggy and the waist is a bit big.  The rest of them aren’t even worth trying.  I’m looking forward to some affordable, high quality, great fitting sweat pants.  Unfortunately, they don’t exist at the moment.  Interesting note, I initially bought all the pants in size large, but they all seemed to fit a bit too tight not only in the waist but throughout the whole let as well.  I like my sweatpants loose fitting so I reordered them all in XL and made my conclusions based on that.Polo Ralph Lauren French RibThey are 100% cotton, which is extremely hard to find.  They may be the heaviest of all the pants (not necessarily good or bad), the most naturally soft (cotton soft compared to nylon “fleece” soft), and the best fit (loose, but not too loose, definitely not tight) throughout the waist and legs, and a good length (long enough that you may walk on the back of them when you’re not wearing shoes).  The inseam is very low however.  That is the one thing I would change.  I’d raise the inseam up by 2 inches.U.S. Polo Assn. Men's Fleece Cargo Pant, Black, LargeNOT AFFILIATED WITH POLO RALPH LAUREN CORP.
U.S. Polo Assn. Men's Fleece Cargo Pant

Also, nylon pants don’t breathe well and cause an uncomfortable and unnecessary sweat.U.S. Polo Assn. Men's Classic Fleece Pant, Dark Grey Heather, LargeNOT AFFILIATED WITH POLO RALPH LAUREN CORP.
U.S. Polo Assn. Men's Classic Fleece Pant

I kept these.  They are a nice loose fit, but the material hasn’t held up as well as the Champion.Russell Athletic Men's Athletic Open-Bottom Pant, Black Heather, Large

These are very light pants.  In fact, I kept them because they were so light.  The size large fits like an XL  compared to all the other pants.  I rarely wear these because they’re so light.Russell Athletic Men's Heavyweight Fleece Open-Bottom Pant - CD1 - L
Russell Athletic Men's Heavyweight Fleece Open-Bottom Pant
The waist band of even the XXL is unbelievable tight.  This must be a design flaw.  It’s unfortunate too because the material was nice and heavy.Russell Athletic Men's Dri-Power Open Bottom Fleece Pocket Pant, Black Heather, Large

I would compare them to the idea of skinny jeans. The sizing and tapering is not generous. I'm not a skinny jeans kind of person. The waist band is still wide and comfortable. They have cuffs at the bottom of the legs. I actually appreciated that, because it doesn't leave gaps, for cold air to enter. But, it won't allow for wearing something like boots. They won't expand enough to pullover the top of the boots. I did find that they are quite good at preventing cold air to penetrate through the material. Except, the interior material against your skin...doesn't have that warm and comfy feel that I expected. It has a bit of a chilling effect. For whatever reason. customer_reviews.title: These Are a New Staple For My Son
customer_reviews.text: Ok, so I’m a fabric snob. I grew up in my mom’s dressmaking shop and from an early age was exposed to and taught about the difference in quality between various fabrics. So I pay close attention to weave, hand-feel, texture and durability of fabrics. Knits can be especially tricky when buying online, because you don’t get any of that tactile insight from a picture. And I’ve “kissed a lot of frogs” when buying knit pieces online. Sometimes the picture looks great, but when the piece arrives, it feels cheap and tacky and plastic-like. Not these sweats!!So…I bought 2 pairs of these sweatpants for my son, and they’re awesome. The fabric on these is super-premium and they look like something I spent $120 on:The deets:-The weave on this fabric is incredibly dense and tight so the hand feel is smooth, and the fabric is weightier than you’re going to get with most other sweatpant brands.-These don’t pill!-The “wrong side” or interior side of the fabric that touches the skin is almost velour-like: it’s soft and super snuggly-I would say these run on the slim side, which is a bonus for us. My son is tall and slender and these have a trim fit to them so they look more polished than most sweatpants (he’s 14, about 5’7” and approximately 122lbs and I bought him a men’s size small)I bought these in black and navy, and I’m going to buy, on repeat, as my son grows. Teenager approved: he loves them and they’re an amazing value for the money.

customer_reviews.title: RL Polo can be some of the best casual wear clothing you can buy
customer_reviews.text: I've been buying Polo socks since the '80s. I've tried numerous other brands and frankly, only Polo -- at least for casual wear -- works for me. I have pairs that I have had for 2 decades. They have shrunk and nowhere near as comfortable as they once were, but they aren't worn and are still wearable. As with anything else Polo, if you can avoid the shrinkage, you've got a good product to wear almost indefinitely. They either stay with the same factories that produce their goods or they keep good controls over the factories they use, unlike other brands. The only real issue with Polo can be price and or value, but these socks were well worth it.I also have a set of black socks that are essentially the same. I wear them with my dress pants and shoes. They are a little thick but are very comfortable. I have all but quit wearing anything higher than quarter socks. My pants do not ride up on my leg so quarter socks do not show and take less time to put on (not a huge deal but if I'm running late...).The one thing I must caution everyone with respect to ANY quality clothing, but ESPECIALLY RL Polo: wash on COLD on Delicate (with a light detergent like Woolite) and then dry on VERY low heat (delicate setting if you have it). If they aren't quite dry, finish the cycle on air dry if you have that setting. Never run these clothes on any hot water or anything but the lowest heat setting in your dryer for as short a period of time as possible. Trust me on this. I have clothing from 20+ years ago that I still wear that has been washed and dried at home. I dry clean some things and a lot of people get their laundry done but it is unlikely you'll do that to these socks. If you throw them in the washer on hot and high heat in the dryer, you'll be lucky to get 6 months out of them. I see 15+ years for mine.

customer_reviews.text: These Under Armour Assert 10s work well as casual work shoes, though they weren't quite up to the task when I started using them for actual running. The Charged Cushioning is comfortable for all-day standing and walking on hard floors, and the breathable mesh upper keeps your feet from overheating during long shifts.For work, the neutral support and lightweight design make them a solid choice. The durability is decent for everyday walking, and they clean up easily when they get dirty. The grip is good on most indoor surfaces, even when dealing with the occasional spill.However, when I started using them for running, their limitations became clear. The cushioning compresses pretty quickly under the impact of regular running, and the support isn't substantial enough for longer distances. After about 50 miles of running, they started to show noticeable wear in the midsole, and the responsiveness diminished significantly.Bottom line: great comfortable shoe for work or casual wear, but serious runners should look elsewhere for their training shoes. Think of these more as athletic-styled work shoes rather than dedicated running shoes.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

I usually wear 9.0 wide (USA), so that is what I ordered and it fit perfectly.- Comfort and Ease. I like how comfortable they are and they are easy to slip on and off (if you wish) by the use of the heel pull tab. The tab also prevents the heel from getting bunched in or broken when putting on the shoes, which was a frequent problem with some other brands I have owned in the past.- Easy to Clean, Quality Mesh. I have seen some reviews saying these shoes wear out easily or the mesh is easier to damage. YMMV but I didn't seem to have this issue and I've had these shoes for about a year. IMO I find the mesh to be much more durable than the cloth mesh most sports shoes have these days and much easier to clean, which is essential for anyone like myself, who often hikes or runs in forestry/mud.- Above Average Quality. As for the year timeframe, the 1st set was about 8 months of extreme use, then I purchased a 2nd pair which I've had for about 3 months now. This may seem like a short timeframe to some but for me, I usually have to change shoes every 6 months or less if they are lower quality because they get a lot of mileage and use. I still have the 1st set which I use as lawn mowing shoes, as they are still usable but the tread does not get much grip/traction anymore for running. I liked them enough to buy that 2nd pair instead of some other brand/model.- Decent Arch Support and Sole Tread. You will find other shoes with the same or better, but I didn't see many that were this cheap in price.- Part of Amazon's Try Before You Buy. Free try-ons. You can take up to 6 days to decide whether to keep/return if you wish, and only be charged if not returned by the 7th day. Day 1 is the day they are delivered.- Uniform in Color. The shoe currently comes in all-black or all-white, including the logo. YMMV but this is a pro for me due to work restrictions requiring all-black shoes, so I can also wear them leisurely at work if I choose (I'm a mechanic). Great for anyone with the same issue, or military, etc.CONs:- Not the most expert/elite quality shoe out there, but will definitely check most people's boxes for average needs, imo.- Cost is higher than one might desire for just simple leisure shoes. But as an avid runner, the price is about average. However, they are usually on sale. My 1st set was around 40% off which dropped it from $70-something to $43, which was worth it for me. 2nd set was about 20% off. Winter holiday seems to be the best time for sales price.- Tread pattern is smooth and circular, instead of rigid and square/triangle, in case that matters to you (in regards to rock climbing etc)Overall I was surprisingly satisfied with this shoe model personally, but your mileage may vary.

I usually wear normal width shoes too, but the fore-foot for the normal width was much too narrow so I had to go to the wide size.  The wide size is fine in the forefoot but a bit too wide in the heel, so again I'm having to adjust the shoe to get it to feel right.  They're better for walking than most other shoes I've tried recently though, so it's worth it to keep working on the insole to get a better fit.

On hard surfaces the nubs make a funny noise and people stared at me obviously amused by my choice of footwear.  They click clacked on the hard tile so not good choice for out and about activities.  Maybe sprinting on clay track or grass turf.  Stay off concrete/asphalt/indoor surfaces.The G. Villas seem nice tennis shoe comparable to my Kswiss Classics so I might try them but I do not need tennis shoes right now.  If I did I would rather G Unit Reebox's.The speed cats piqued my interest some time ago but I was not sure if the sleek styling was suitable for casual wear, too European.  I could definitely see the value as sports trainers am I really liked when the outsole was good year rubber tire inspired.  Kind of like racing car slicker tires i.e. less tread more traction.  Now I am into working out more so these would be more appropriate for me as long as I did not combine the with no show socks as is a current trend.  I need coverage on my Achilles plus like wearing Nike quarter crews so you can SEE the logo.  No show's have logo on bottom of sock wear you can not see it, how stupid is that.All in all these are probably the best puma I have had not to low like the speed cats which would have to be purely sports trainers.  I can wear these with jeans and look cool like they are Adidas superstars or something.  Low shoes look bad with jeans unless you are bisexual and wear tight jeans or something.  I wear looser jeans so low shoes tend to be paired training shorts.  I can bench press with loose jeans and look normal.So these worked for the money , look good for casual, knocked off the Asics Corsair's/Nike Cortez but as least incorporated a leather tongue which should be almost mandatory, and are okay for sports and training.  Not hardcore running or atg squats but bench pressing, leg pressing, light track work etc.Update 8/9/2019:I just received a white with black stripe. They are not as good as the originals. They are lighter and cheap naugahyde. They had a scratch on one and the other was crushed. They are comfortable but not the quality I expect from a german brand. Very cheap chinese feel.

customer_reviews.title: Surprise in the Snow
customer_reviews.text: I purchased this shoe as well as a pair of the Skecher Afterburn M tennis shoes.  I wanted a dedicated work shoe, because I was going though my shoes pretty quickly from wearing the same pair all the time.  So, being that I had already had two previous pairs of the “Afterburn” shoe, and burned through each of them in just over a year respectively, I decided to get another pair of them and also get a pair of the Cessnock Food Service Shoe strictly for work.  Both pairs of shoes arrived yesterday, and today I wore the Food Service shoe (FSS) to work for the first time.I slipped them on and found them to be a perfect fit.  They are very light weight and comfortable.  Usually, I find new shoes need a few days of wear to break-in until they really conform to the shape of your foot and then begin to fit well, but that wasn’t the case with these FSS shoes; they fit perfectly the moment I put them on.I wore them all day at work and discovered something that really surprised me.  We had a snowstorm today and got about 2” by the time I got to work, and had a good 7” by the end of my shift.  I park outside so of course I have to brush the snow off the car.  After doing so I knocked the snow off my shoes before getting into the car.  I was surprised to see that the snow didn’t stick to the material on top of the shoes, it was as if there was a water repellant in/on the material.  I was sort of wondering why my feet weren’t getting cold while I was cleaning off my car and I guess that explains it.  Another surprise was the fact that these shoes make no sound when walking on a tile floor while having wet soles.  The “Afterburn” tennis shoes squeak like a rusty hinge when the bottom of the shoe is wet and you walk across tile or other such surfaces, but the FSS’s, are quiet as a mouse, not a sound comes from them, you could almost call them Ninja shoes.As for the style, well that’s a personal preference and these shoes suit me just fine.  I think they look sharp, and nobody even noticed I had a new pair of shoes on today.Durability is the unanswered question and being that I’ve only worn them one day, that question will remain unanswered for a while.  If I can get a solid two years out of them, just wearing them to work, I will definitely buy them again and certainly would recommend them to a friend.I hope this review helps with your decision.  Peace.

customer_reviews.title: 2023 UPDATE - DANG THEY ENDURED A LOT (A FRESH 2020 REVIEW!!! - Yeah, they're pretty good.)
customer_reviews.text: I wanted to leave a review for these shoes specifically because Amazon has a habit of throwing old reviews at the buyer rather than more recent ones. There aren't many with a fair critique, or they resort to omg it sucks/rocks. So, here we go.After years of using TredSafe shoes due to just not having the money to afford fancy-shmancy, I bit the bullet on these shoes figuring I could at least default to other shoes if they didn't work out. Also, a lot of reviews complained on durability and such, but they were recommended, so I went for it.Durability: Uhhhh, folks must have run over their pairs with a lawn mower to get them wrecked like they were, because wow have mine been accidentally kicked into and scraped by a LOT of old metal equipment and hardware with basically no damage. Really, the only damage was a screw I somehow stepped on, drilling a hole into the bottom. I mean, it didn't poke my foot, so no harm done.Comfort: Okay, so memory foam is a big your mileage may vary situation, but generally the foam is pretty okay in these shoes. Seeing as I run around a lot more at my new job than I did my old one, these do pretty good at cushioning my 13W feet. Then again, I am also a tall dude, so the memory foam cushioning may not be as effective for me. It hasn't been long enough to really wear it out either, but again, your mileage may vary. Also depends on whether you really understand memory foam, which I kind of don't. I might be totally off-base.But anyways. Even without that, the general feel and support of the shoe is good. The fact that my heels basically never hurt after eight-hour shifts when they would tend to hurt in the old, cheap TredSafe shoes is a pretty good testament to that fact.The fit: It fits...? I mean, 13W feet, I bought 13W. It fit pretty much as expected. The only minor complaint I can make is more a special case: there isn't a lot of room for inserts. See, I'm weird and have a tendency to put more pressure on the front of my feet than the heel, and not a shoe can be found at reasonable price for someone weird like me. I'd like to be able to fit some front support into the shoes to counter that, but there's just not enough room. Maybe once I wear out the memory foam, but otherwise... Well, that's a me thing. If you walk like a normal person rather than like I did as a kid to catch late-night TV without being caught, then you should be okay.Other stuff: One other minor complaint is just a typical sneaker issue but a bit worse. When the bottoms of the shoes get wet, walking on any kind of hard floor gives off an obnoxious squeaking sound. I don't mean like basketball court squeaking. I mean like twisting leather squeaking. To be fair... They're sneakers. They'll make noise like that, but it's usually not that annoying. They do dry out pretty quick so long as you don't keep getting them wet, so it doesn't last particularly long.So... Four stars? Yeah. They're pretty good overall, and they sure do take a beating. I keep expecting something I do to rip it open, but there isn't a single tear or crack anywhere (besides the hole from the screw). Main problem is just memory foam getting in the way of using inserts, lack of front foot support for those like yours truly, and the obnoxious wet squeak. Still a solid shoe, though. Worth the money.Update: 07/22/2023Just bought a second pair because the pair I use finally showed signs of serious wear, which is pretty impressive since I've used these shoes for almost everything from job work to yard work. They have had their soles handed to them regularly and only just now started actually falling apart in any measure. They aren't dead just yet, but the shoes were on a good sale so I bought pair two ahead of time.I did end up wearing out the memory foam rather quick (but I also walk weird, so once again your mileage may vary) but pulling them out to replace with new inserts was really easy, so it was a simple swap-out. I will say it's best to just swap for more memory foam since other support inserts didn't help just because of the shoe's own support.So yeah, running back in to say you REALLY have to try to destroy these shoes to make them fall apart: for having lasted 3 years of me, they've done a very good job staying together. They're still comfortable, pretty good support, and make the annoying leather-twisting noise when wet, but I definitely think they're worth the price, sale or not.

customer_reviews.title: I'm disappointed in the advertising message on the tongue of the shoe, but these are very good shoes
customer_reviews.text: I've been wearing Brooks Adrenaline GTS shoes for 8 years, and during that time have bought multiple pairs of 3 different models of GTS shoes.  They are really good shoes, very comfortable, I can very easily wear then all day long (more comfortable than just wearing socks around the house), and perfect for the particular pronation of my feet.  However, this is the first time I've purchased the 2024 edition of these shoes (the Adrenaline GTS 24), and I'm disappointed to discover that there is now a conspicuous advertising message on the tongue of the shoes.  In a bold black stripe, it says Adrenaline 24 GTS, which is eye-catching and detracts from the appearance of the shoes.  On the GTS 18 and GTS 16 models of these shoes, the branding on the tongue of the shoe was very subtle, which I like.  But with these GTS 24 shoes, it's kind of like wearing a big NIKE message on the front of my shirt or something.  Part of the reason I chose this un-flashy gray color is so my shoes will blend in with any casual outfit I wear, but with these shoes, I feel like I'm making a big statement to the world that I love my Brooks Adrenaline GTS shoes.  The bold black stripe is made of a spandex material, and is only sewn-in on the ends of the stripe, so I guess I could use some scissors to cut it off.  But then there would be this little messy black edge where I cut off the advertising.  Anyway, bummer about the bold black advertising stripe, and I hope they omit this in future models of this shoe.  But it's still a really good shoe.

customer_reviews.title: You might like these if 100% synthetic is not a problem for you
customer_reviews.text: I like to wear my sneakers without socks.  Not these.  100% synthetic equals hydrophobic!  In other words, the materials used (polyester and plastic) to produce these don't like moisture.  They don't breathe well and they make your feet sweat.  I have to take them off after 30 minutes of wearing them with no socks.  Although they are quite comfortable, I need to wear low-cut socks to help with the moisture management if I know I am going to have them on for a long duration.  These shoes are budget-priced sneakers and are not made with the highest quality materials so they don't offer great support.  I am happy to kick them off after wearing them for an entire afternoon.  One final item, the inner soles of mine were not attached to the bottom of the shoe so when I did try wearing them without socks, the soles would stick to my feet and come out of the shoes as I took the sneakers off.  Really annoying.  Was this a QC issue with my pair or simply a design flaw in the shoe?  I have no idea but I don't like that the soles come out every time I remove the shoes.

customer_reviews.title: Good foam but really finnicky upper
customer_reviews.text: You don't have to look that far to see the Nimbus get recommended on sites and YouTube videos. I can see why they do, it's a easy shoe to run in, to walk in. It has a nice bounce but it gets 3 stars because the fit is disastrous. I do regret buying them and wish I went with something else.I have bought the right size, snug but correct length, but yet my heel gets cut and rubbed against! The heel doesn't slip, it actually doesn't move at all but digs into me. It's actually not unheard of if you do a search for others with similar issues. I have found the cause to be lacing the shoes too tight. Especially towards the toes, and it's better to relax lacing so your feet can fit inside the shoe deeper towards the front, giving room for the heel.In my process of trying to find the right fit from lacing, thicker socks, I also tried without socks, and if you look at my picture there's a lot of sharp edges inside that cut you! Yes the answer is to always wear socks, but I realized my favorite pair of running pants started pilling towards the front ankle because of this shoe! It was rubbing and scratching the front hem of my pants. (I tuck the hem in now on runs).When these shoes Work it does a great job on a run, they can get a bit heavy after awhile, they are on the heavier side as far as running shoes go, but great foam cushioning. They require a bit of break in width wise, a bit narrow initially.I wish I would want to reach for these even when I'm not running, but sadly they aren't my gotos for groceries or chores because they just aren't comfortable on the uppers. It's only through a lot of experimenting did I find them to be acceptable.

Also, I was in a fast food restaurant while they were mopping the floor, and I walked outside the wet area where there was simply a lightly damp area, and I slide as thought I was on a skating rink. I love the style and fit of the shoe until I start walking. It appears there may be a quality control problem. I've read numerous reviews about the issue and yet it continues to be a problem. I changing my rating from a 5 to a 3. I hope the company will correct the issue, because the shoe is a great shoe! The shoes were made in India. I do believe that my problem is not everyone's problem, and every shoe manufactured does not have this problem, therefore, I am still recommending the shoe with a 3 rating.

customer_reviews.title: Eureka!  A comfortable shoe!
customer_reviews.text: At a certain point in life, a man reaches a deeper understanding.  A viewpoint that permanently alters his worldview, and makes him question all that came before.  This can happen slowly, as experience and knowledge grows, and ultimately crystalizes around a kernel of this new perspective.  Or it can happen suddenly, in an epiphany of recognition that forces a foundational frame of reference adjustment.  Yesterday I experienced the latter, and I wanted to share it in case any of you have yet to reach a similar point.  As enter the fall of life, I feel compelled to offer this new personal world order in the hope that you may benefit longer than I will likely enjoy.While this change thunder-struck me suddenly yesterday, some background will help put the revelation in proper context.  It all started with the bankruptcy of Sears.  Sears engaged in a foolhardy acquisition strategy during the 1980's of retail and non-retail businesses that would be completely undercut by the digital revolution of the 1990's.  The debt accumulated from these various acquisitions would drag on company financial statements for decades as revenues slowly eroded to online shopping alternatives.  Finally, in the face of an unmanageable October 2018 debt payment of $134 million, Sears declared Chapter 11.  Eddie Lampert made several attempts to secure funding for a reorganization strategy, but they would all ultimately fail.  None of this impacted me until the end of 2019 when the last Sears in Jacksonville closed.At that point I had a shoe problem.  For decades I had purchased brown four-hole lace-up suede loafers from Sears.  They were a store brand that sold for $30 or $40.  I had probably purchased a dozen or more pair of these.  I would often buy two or three pair at a time so I wouldn't need to return to the store so often as they wore out.  But now Sears and my default shoe choice were gone!  Panic ensued.  I started searching the internet for the manufacturer of this shoe which I had enjoyed for so many years.  The hope was that another distribution channel would emerge, or that a transition to online sales could be found.  No luck.  So at the dawn of COVID-19, I was facing an existential shoe crisis.It was about March 2020 when my last trusty Sears loafers were at end-of-life.  Most real world retail was shuttered, and supply chain disruption was in full force.  There were no shoes to buy.  Finally, a local Rack Room reopened and I scoured the shelves for a suitable replacement.  I eventually settled for a deck style shoe that was only mildly stylistically objectionable, but seemed acceptably comfortable as one of the very few models offered in wide width.  For nearly two and a half years this daily worn (weekday) pair of shoes sustained me.  Last week I was forced back to the retail experience for a hopefully improved selection of casual shoe options.Did I find an improved post-COVID selection?  Hell no, I did not!  It was WAY worse.  There were no wide offerings at all!  Three shoe store visits left me cursing the pathetic state of IRL retail, and the stupid business people who were essentially forcing me to shop online.  So home to Amazon I went, with the name of an untried shoe brand and model seen in a store.  It was a pleasing looking set of footwear that I was going to gamble might be suitable.  And the size variety available on Amazon was breathtaking.  All the sizes I was familiar with, that were completely missing from any store, were available with a click.  I don't know when stores decided that they couldn't offer size selection.  They certainly did in the 1970's!  How did they lose that ability?  Anyway, shoes selected and ordered online with delivery anticipated in a couple days.  Fine.Ladies and gentleman, this is it.  These Rockport Oxford Eureka Walking Shoes are THE most comfortable shoes I have ever owned...bar none.  I am gobsmacked by how comfortable these shoes are.  Eureka is right!  I think back to pre-Rockport me and shake my head in sorrow.  Poor fella.  Stuck in a rut of frugally driven brick-and-mortar retail based consumption resulting in the bare minimum of utility.  Not even guessing about the possibility that such a paradigm shift could be out there.  Who knows what might have been if that version of me had found these shoes earlier?  Years of an improved outlook on life is the most obvious missed opportunity.  Perhaps he would have turned to philanthropy?  Trying to engineer life improvements for those around him in an effort to induce similar outlook-altering reactions in society's less fortunate?  I literally skipped around the house yesterday sharing the good news with my family.  I haven't skipped since a 1973 visit to Cedar Point with my Aunt Fran.  Eureka my friends.  Eureka indeed.  If you're in need, I beg you to give these shoes a try.  If I can convince just one of you, then this lunchtime prose will have been worth it.Edit: Two year update on durability - These spectacular shoes have been part of my workday fit for two years now.  No major durability issues to report.  The highest wear was on the insole.  The soles still have quite a bit of life, and are still well attached to the uppers.  One black pair I bought has fully thrown their insoles, and the brown pair have significantly worn insoles.  I still feel that this wear pattern is above average compared to my past shoe purchases.  So much so, I just ordered another pair of both black and brown Rockport Oxford Eureka Walking Shoes.  Love 'em, and looking forward to the fresh kicks!

customer_reviews.title: Great, long lasting, very durable shoes.  Break-in required.
customer_reviews.text: These are awesome shoes.  They last for a very long time.  They run a bit tight, and pretty stiff.  I use old-school techniques, that I learned in the Army, for new Rockports.  I put them on, and wear them for an hour.  I'm not going to lie, they chew on my feet pretty hard for that hour.  Then I wear them for a couple of hours, on some errands that require walking.  They start out biting pretty hard, but after a couple of hours, they feel like a good pair of gloves, and they're like walking on clouds.  The third time, I wear them to work.  I pack a spare pair of shoes, in case my feet get too sore, but they usually don't.  After that third day, they might be a little hard to put on, but once on, they're super comfortable.  I have a pair that are 5 years old, still look great for office work, and are one of two pairs of shoes that I go to when I know I'm going to be on my feet a lot.  It's a process to break them in, but good leather requires break in.  These shoes are worth it!

customer_reviews.title: Quality trouble - exceptional customer service!
customer_reviews.text: My husband has been wearing Rockports for over 30 years - never had a problem before.  These have been worn only a few months - both have the same problem - soles separating and flapping when he walks.  VERY disappointed - what happened to Rockport quality?Could have been a bad batch of glue?I took photos and contacted Rockport directly on their website late in the afternoon (well past 7 pm eastern time) - and received a sympathetic and apologetic response within FIVE minutes! They said they would send me replacement shoes but couldn’t find details of my order (I’d bought in US on Amazon and was contacting Rockport Canada). I sent a copy of my Amazon invoice and explained where I’d bought and thought they’d use that as the reason they couldn’t help - but NO - another response in less than five minutes - they would forward to warranty department and I should hear from them. Which I did - less than an hour later! They didn’t have the same shoe in stock - but a gift card for the purchase price was an option or select a different style - just let them know. I have never received such excellent online customer service. I believe in supporting companies that stand behind their products and provide service - especially prompt and sympathetic service! I have changed my review from 1 star to 5.

customer_reviews.title: 600 treadmill miles per pair
customer_reviews.text: I've been through 4 pairs now. I have a treadmill desk and log all miles carefully, so I can say confidently I put on 400-450 miles of treadmill use on each pair, plus they are my daily driver so probably closer to 650 miles per year.I echo all the positive remarks about slip resistance, easy to put on, cushioned without feeling like I'm on a balloon, and subdued but professional appearance.On durability, I'm a little disappointed that they only last a year, but this was the first shoe I've tried on my treadmill desk, so I'm not sure how it compares to other shoes.In any case, every shoe has eventually failed in the same way, after a year of constant use: the plastic shaper in the heel falls apart and starts poking at my heel, and the cover of the foam insert disintegrates in a way that starts to wear my socks out quickly. It took me three pairs to realize that's why my expensive socks weren't lasting as long as they should.All said, I'll buy them again. They fit really well and look nice and are very comfortable to walk hundreds of miles in. I'll just need to remember to buy new ones every year!

customer_reviews.title: Terrific Security Shoes!
customer_reviews.text: This might not be brief, but it will be efficient (and worth it)!1. I bought/tried these shoes because, within six months, I have always ripped the front of my new balance shoes (for ~ a decade) requiring new ones. Hence I waited 1 year + to write this review...2. These shoes are as comfortable as new balance and still look new! So no need to constantly replace them... Or baby them (I'm hard on shoes).As you can imagine the steel keeps the front of the shoe from ripping. So never again...3. I run (with my dog -- fast) in these shoes, they are that comfortable.4. Therefore they are perfect from a security perspective. Not only can no one stomp on your foot and do you harm, but imagine getting kicked with these suckers on! Also, you could run away if you needed to...5. These shoes are so comfortable, I routinely think I'm wearing my slippers and thus fail to swap them when I get home. I've caught myself many times realizing I wore them all day.6. I made a mistake when I bought my first pair. I knew I would get lazy and not change shoes to walk my dog, so I wanted to avoid smashing my toes against the steel plate during a run. If you're a runner of any distance, you know how much damage that can do to your feet. So I bought 10s instead of 9.5. Four months later I bought 9.5 because they clearly accounted for that in the design. And the 10s were too big. My feet were sliding around too much in those, even with pads in them.7. They are roomy vertically so I doubled up some pads in them (the 9.5s) thus increasing their comfort. Yet they remain roomy/comfortable. I never bump up against the plate.8. You can put HEAVY things on them, I often hang drywall, and you can set it on your shoes feeling no pressure on your feet while keeping the drywall off the ground.9. They are a tad on the warm side. Terrific in winter, and even good for walking in snow, but in the summer, on a hot day my feet will sweat. Not wonderful. They breathe, but there are tradeoffs. IE It's hard to breathe through a steel plate. So I can't blame the manufacturer, I still love them.10. The sole is not particularly flexible, it doesn't exactly conform/bend to your feet during a run, but I wouldn't think buyers of shoes like these would care.  I got used to it, but it's worth mentioning in case others might (care). And that leads to my next point:11. During a run, a sharp rock came up through the bottom of my first pair. I was shocked because that never happened before. And I suspect the ridgidness of the sole may have contributed. They weren't destroyed by that, but if you're walking around a construction site, be careful. Safe on top, not so sure about the bottom. In a year + that hasn't happened with this pair. They're not bad soles, but perhaps the only room for improvement.12. I never thought someone stomping on my foot could do me harm. I thought that was ridiculous in movies until I dropped something heavy on my foot 2 years ago. Wow - ouch! So even if you don't do construction, these are a great upgrade to your personal security for that reason alone.13. Even with the steel plate and sturdy construction, I don't find them all that heavy (anymore), but they are heavier and a bit clunky, runners will notice and it took some getting used to. Eventually my laziness, about changing shoes, won out and now I'm used to running in them. And I no longer view them as such a drag. For several months, I loathed running in them until one day I just forgot.14. I don't consider them waterproof. Water resistant maybe, but don't sell your waders. Your feet will get wet if you submerge them.15. If you want shoes that will last forever, look good without maintenance, increase your personal security, protect your feet, and that you will eventually find very comfortable, these are for you.

customer_reviews.title: Good, solid, comfortable shoes but very, very heavy.
customer_reviews.text: I got tired of my normal athletic shoes going bad from the stress of daily use on the job, so I went looking under the search term durable work shoes.  (Looking via Duck and Swisscows and Qwant, mind you, not via Amazon's own search fields, which, inexplicably, continue to be left as almost 100% useless.)Inevitably, nothing that was classified as a.) a shoe and b.) durable was available without a steel toe, so I relented and bought these.  For the record:  The heaviest thing I'm likely to drop on my feet is a disk of Lanthanum/Telluride alloy (or maybe Silicon/Germanium,) that's roughly the size, shape and weight of a U.S. Nickel, so I'm not really in need of steel-toed shoes.  But if you want durable, apparently you have to get the Medieval Class toe box, so I just bought them.I don't know if it's just the steel toe or a combination of that and the heavier-duty rubber and upper material, but these shoes are seriously heavy.  Not a big problem if you like the added exercise, but it would be great if shoe manufacturers would offer a version of the exact same work shoe with all of the exact same materials, but without the mëtal hardware.  But I knew that going in so...These are excellent shoes despite the weight.  I have wide feet and they're available in EE width (if they hadn't been I simply would not have bought them, because you can't be cool if your feet are uptight, as the old Hush Puppies ad used to say.)  They're built like tanks but are perfectly comfortable nonetheless, and I'm on my feet roughly 80% of every nine-hour workday.I got my normal size and width, and even with a pair of podiatrist-prescribed orthotic inserts and Odor-Eater pads, they fit perfectly.  When I put them on in the morning the toe areas do feel tight, but the inserts settle within minutes and they're a perfect fit thereafter.  So be aware that if you do not use any kind of insert these might be a little roomy.  The laces are also heavy-duty and the eyelets for them allow you to tighten them without messing with the loop-by-loop finger-pull thing - but neither do they let loose too easily - all of which I like lots.Given the excellent price, durability and fit, I'm really happy that I picked these.  Time will tell how well they'll hold up, but I've been wearing them on the job for two months and they still look and feel brand-new. I'm on hands and knees and crawling into the guts of systems and lab equipment frequently, and though the inevitable dirt is there, I don't even see so much as a scuff on the outer surfaces, anywhere.  Good shoes, if seriously heavy in the weight class.

customer_reviews.title: Great work shoes for construction, warehouse jobs, etc
customer_reviews.text: Great for working in a warehouse. Very protective. I can kick heavy stuff without hurting my foot if I curl my toes slightly. I've used my shoes to avoid pinching my fingers when setting down heavy objects, to get pallet jacks unstuck from pallets by holding the pallet in place with my foot, and to get old rusty latches on delivery vans open by kicking the lever. I know from experience that the steel toe can support over 1,000lbs, just don't tell my boss how I figured that out....I'm not sure how protective they are when it comes to stepping on nails, but I'll let update my review if I find out! (Stepping on nails sticking up out of boards isn't exactly a rare occurrence in warehouse and construction environments)They're surprisingly water resistant. Stepping in puddles, walking through snow, and even pressure-washing vehicles doesn't get my feet wet. They're quite grippy, and the tread on the soles doesn't seem to wear down. While wearing these, I've only ever slipped on ice and soapy concrete, never on wet wood, concrete floor, metal, etc.They're certainly not comfort shoes, but they're comfortable enough for work. Better than broken toes! They're not light, but they don't feel particularly heavy. I'm still fairly agile while wearing them, they're not great for running, but I can run in them comfortably and without tripping. It's quite comfortable to rest one foot on top of the other while sitting, since the shoes don't bend too easily like sneakers do.They're very durable, aside from the memory foam insoles, which develop holes pretty quickly, although you really can't feel the holes. In my experience, they last about 8 months, which is decent, considering they're relatively inexpensive and stand up to a lot. My first pair had a bit of peeling rubber on the front and the holes in the insoles had gotten quite deep, so I replaced them, although they're still wearable as a backup option. I just bought replacements for my second pair, which are actually in pretty good shape other than the inside of the left shoe wearing down, causing the hard protective layer inside to rub on my heel and cause minor discomfort while walking.The sizing seems accurate. I have fairly wide feet, and wear size 13 in most brands, sometimes 14 (eg, Under Armour). The size 13-Wide fits perfectly, with just enough room for my toes to not be squished together like they are in most shoes.9/10, would recommend these for anyone with the risk of injuring their feet at work.

customer_reviews.title: Great shoes.  Fit big feet.  Comfortable.  Don't feel like clogs/slippers.
customer_reviews.text: Edit to add: These do have horrible traction in wet/snow.  Use extreme caution on wet floors, and just don't wear if it's snowy/icy.  I'm removing 1 star for that, because I had to get a different pair of shoes for bad weather.  (Telluride Moc, which are better for traction, but not as comfortable.)  That said, I'm on my 3rd pair of these, and for regular office work, they're great.Original:Why did I not buy these sooner?TL;DR: Great shoes.  Fit big feet.  Comfortable.  Don't feel like clogs/slippers.I am someone who values my time and..... oh hell... I'm lazy.  I slip my shoes off by holding down the heel with the other foot, and put them on before leaving for work by sticking my foot back in.  As such, I tend to destroy the heels of all my shoes.(I'm a computer tech, so I mostly wear sneakers or "casual" shoes)For years I'd thought about getting these sort of shoes, and for years I'd held off because I have huge feet (15) and usually only new balance fit my foot correctly without a break-in period.I can now say there's an exception to that rule.  I got the 14s of these the first time around, because people said they ran big.  Not so.  14 was too small, so I went to 15, and they're perfect.  They also have arch support that at first felt weird, but now feels like something I don't know how I lived without.  They have also felt like a broken-in pair since the first (maybe second) day I wore them.If I have any complaint, it's that they pick up a TON of sand/salt/ice/snow in the tread and keep dropping it for a good half hour once you get to your destination in winter.  At home I take off my shoes at the door, but I notice it at work when my chair is crunching over sand from the parking lot.Most importantly, however, I've been wearing these for a couple weeks now, all day, every day, and they still slip on and off with ease, but don't feel floppy on my feet when I'm walking over weird terrain.  If I had any wish, I guess it'd be that they make a pair with mesh in the toe area.  They do get a little warm at times, but I don't see an easy way to do that with the design.Overall.... well, I guess the fact that I'm planning to buy a second pair speaks for itself.

customer_reviews.title: Nice for the price.
customer_reviews.text: For reference my husband is 6’2, 205 pounds with broad shoulders, long arms, long legs, and a short torso. He wears a 44L in men’s suits and 36W/34L (pants). His neck is 17.5”. So WTS, here’s how it fit:The jacket is a perfect fit particularly across the back of his shoulders. He can button the top button closest to his neck without feeling chocked/restricted. The arms fall right at the break of his wrists. However, there’s too much room around the waist area but that’s because he’s more narrow at the bottom. The problem is that it causes the slits on the back of the jacket to gap open which looks kinda funky so I’ll have to have it altered for a more tailored look. I will add that the fabric is very nice, not too heavy and the jacket is lined.As for the pants, they are paper thin (see through) and soft. The wooden button is a little difficult to use, as he got tired of trying to dislodge it so he ended up carefully pulling the pants off with them buttoned. The pants fall slightly above his ankles, and the fit is definitely snug around the waist, butt and thighs. My husband also has runner’s thighs and is not comfortable wearing tight or fitted clothing but this is how they’re supposed to fit. So yeah, it’ll take him a minute to get used to it but he only has to wear this for a few hours so he’ll be fine. So IMO the pants are fine but be forewarned that if your (or his) waist is 38+ the pants could potentially be a problem.The colors are like a sherbet coral, creamy white and soft blue. The quality is good and it was delivered in 2 days. Thus far, I have no regrets about this purchase. I hope this helps as there weren’t a lot of reviews at the time of my purchase.

customer_reviews.title: Nice for a business casual office

On my softness scale of 1-5, I would give it a 4.25. It has not bothered my sensitive skin. It did not shrink or bleed color in the laundering, nor did it pick up excess lint. There is a tiny bit of twisting, but not sure it's even enough that would be noticed. customer_reviews.text: I wanted to post an initial review in case anyone like me has events this weekend and is considering buying this.TL; Dr: these shaper shorts are great if you're looking for light compression/support and some smoothing.As a tall plus size woman (5'11, 310lbs, 50-46-56, usually wear a 3x/4x), this item suits my needs to look a bit smoother under clingy dresses, prevent thigh chafing, and provide some abdominal compression for POTS symptoms relief. I have my highschool reunion this weekend and will be wearing a bodycon dress, so I wanted some shaper shorts that would smooth me out a bit without being uncomfortable. The mixed reviews on this item scared me a bit, but so far I'm glad I took a chance. I've been wearing them to work the past couple of days to test them out in case I needed to switch sizes or to another brand.These shaper shorts are surprisingly comfortable for having a decent amount of light-modedate compression. While I'm tall, I'm also quite short-waisted with a long hip/pelvis, and carry most of my weight in my stomach, butt, and upper thighs. The waistband comes all the way up to my bra line, but so far has not rolled down thanks to the fabric quality and small stays strategically placed. The legs are also a great length to not roll on my thick thighs - I'm easily able to adjust them higher or lower depending on the length of my skirt. The fabric is fairly breathable and soft, doesn't irritate my sensitive skin. Other than the very top of the waistband, I can't feel them on after a bit.I'm glad I went with the 4x instead of the 3x. My measurements were on the low end of the 4x, and I decided to opt for comfort over stronger compression. The shorts are quite stretchy, and I imagine someone several inches bigger than me could comfortably wear them. The shorts washed fine in a laundry bag on delicate cycle and didn't shrink too much. I can't speak to their long-term durability and performance, but I will update this review after my events with pictures and final thoughts.Overall, I definitely can recommend these to others looking for similar qualities in shaper shorts. I hope this review helps other tall plus size women as I know how hard it is to find comfortable, flattering clothing for us.

customer_reviews.title: Possible Merchant Error
customer_reviews.text: Lots of the reviews described the product being too big when ordering the size according to the chart. The shorts fit, but they didn't really provide the support expected. On the advice of a few, I purchased a size xs/s instead of m/l like I normally do.When I looked at the shorts, I thought there was no way that I was going to be able to fit my skinny-squishy 165lb body in those itty-bitty things. But I did. And without much effort at all.  They're tight, but they're not snatching my waist like they're supposed to. Everything is smoothed out. No bulges. And I can breathe, but it didn't shape my stomach. My stomach is still pooching out like it did before. There's just smooth flub-blub now instead of multiple flub-blubs and no muffin top (which is nice).I sat down on the bed to see if it was possible to still breathe (it was) and I looked at the package. On the back of the package it says Plus-size black small and it now makes sense why I am able to wear it.I'm 5'11. 165lbs. All of my weight is in my stomach, hips, and thighs. I wear a size 10-12 in jeans.Plus-sized clothing is made specifically to accommodate a body type that is beautifully voluptuous. Plus-sized clothing is labeled 16W or 16 curvy fur example.  The W or curvy indicating that it will fit a fuller figured individual. I know there's not a small in plus-size, but I think I've figured it out nonetheless:I have a friend that wears a size 14 curvy which is another way to tell the shopper that this product is constructed differently from a size 14 regular. The curvy or the W are constructed in a way that allows a fuller figure to settle comfortably unlike the regular that would be far too tight and constricting in the waiste, knees, and calves. Anyway...I checked on Amazon and found a plus-size Shapermint, high waisted shaper shorts that can be purchased in size S-3xl. These shorts are made like the curvy or W to accommodate curves that a woman who wore a regular small would not have. I believe the seller may have accidentally shipped a plus-sized garment when the purchaser wanted a regular rather than plus. And I think that this is why some buyers are talking about sizing down while others are describing being swallowed by a boa constrictor and not being able to breathe, or move, or sit.Maybe if I had a regular small then I'd be complaining about that, too because, trust me, I may be skinny-squishy but I haven't been able to fit into a small anything since 9th grade. And that was 32 years ago.
